Access and exemption regimes vary by jurisdiction; the model carries markings, bases and review dates but never a statutory interpretation.
Register publicity conventions differ sharply between civil-law public registers and common-law custodial registers; the model records publicity status as data.
ISO 15489/23081 and RiC-CM are treated as the international backbone.
US 36 CFR/44 U.S.C. definitions apply only when the adopting Dimension asserts US Federal jurisdiction.
eIDAS signature levels apply when the adopting Dimension asserts EU/EEA trust-service law.
C2PA is optional and currently most relevant to media and generated-content assets in adopting markets.
Language of description defaults to the record's content language; multilingual titles are allowed via localized strings.
RFC 3339 timestamps with explicit offset or Z are required even where local records law still uses date-only cutoffs; date-only values should be normalized with an explicit policy, not inferred.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether version and instantiation can collapse into one concept: rejected. A format migration changes bytes and digests without changing content, and PREMIS and RiC-O both keep the layers apart; collapsing them would make every migration look like an amendment.

Tested whether the archival aggregation belongs in this model: rejected. RiC-O models RecordSet as a distinct class and the registry already assigns aggregation to WM-REC-015; only membership references are retained here.

Tested whether signature validity can be a static attribute: rejected. Validity depends on the validation moment, the policy, revocation data and algorithm strength, so it is recorded as a dated outcome with its own artifact, and untimestamped manifests are treated as expiring.

Searched for counterexamples to 'every record has a version chain': born-final register entries, receipts and immutable ledger entries have exactly one version, so version cardinality is 1..n and a single-version record is normal rather than exceptional.

Tested whether document equals file: rejected. One record can span many files and one file can carry many records (compound PDFs, mailboxes, case bundles), which is why storage location is a reference and identity is never a path or a digest.

Tested whether retention can be modelled without holds: rejected. A hold must take precedence over an in-force schedule and requires its own separately authorised release, so disposal scheduling and disposal holding are modelled as distinct concerns, as MoReq2010 does.

Tested whether an inline-only finding was being used to dodge the artifact requirement: each of the four inline-only findings (identity anchor, designation, responsibility roles, status, temporal anchors) points to the artifact elsewhere in the model that evidences it, rather than claiming no evidence exists.

Checked whether disposition can erase its own evidence: rejected. Audit trail, holds and disposition certificates are stored under separate custody and outlive the record, otherwise destruction would be unauditable.
Would a filename, object-storage key or 'document date' be accepted as the master identifier? The model forbids it; identity finding requires a typed scheme.
Would converting PDF to PDF/A mint a new record identity or only a rendition? Format-of versus version-of is an explicit question; conversion is a migration event.
Would deleting the last working copy while a preservation AIP remains be logged as record destruction? Last-copy and package-role questions block that collapse.
Would a C2PA soft binding or watermark be used as the record id? Explicitly forbidden; soft bindings are lookup hints.
Would releasing one of two overlapping holds authorize destruction? Remaining-active-hold-ids must be empty.
Would a custodian's register rights be treated as ownership or as a right to grant public access? Stewardship and access default_rule keep owner as grantor.
Would an unscheduled US Federal record appear on a destroy worklist? Unscheduled-treat-as-permanent is a first-class status.
Would a certified extract that omits annexes keep the original record id? Certified-copy finding forces a same-identity versus new-extract choice.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Providers disagree (claude=aggregate, grok=entity) and the disagreement is resolved in favour of aggregate. Versions, instantiations, signatures, custody intervals, hold assignments and disposition evidence have no independent identity or lifecycle outside the record, and the model's hardest invariants are consistency boundaries that span them: a hold must block disposition across every instantiation, disposition must leave a tombstone that outlives the children, and identity must survive migration and rendition change. Grok's 'entity' reading is contradicted by its own last-copy and overlapping-hold checks, which are aggregate-scoped invariants. Aggregation into record sets stays outside the boundary and remains WM-REC-015, which both providers assert independently.

decisions.concept: Base provider selection
decisions.rationale: Claude's boundary notes name seven actual sibling models (WM-REC-015, agent, naming, time, communication, dataset, file/object storage) with a sourced distinction for each; Grok's notes are largely standards-alignment statements rather than model boundaries. Claude also carries the sibling-excluding out-of-scope list that a deterministic synthesizer needs. Size was not the deciding factor.

decisions.concept: Entry kind aggregate vs entity
decisions.rationale: Holds, last-copy destruction and tombstone survival are invariants that span versions, instantiations and evidence objects; only an aggregate root gives them a consistency boundary. Grok's own adversarial checks assume that boundary while its declared entry kind denies it.

decisions.concept: Capture threshold and record status (grok document-versus-record)
decisions.rationale: Materially absent from the base, which begins after the object is already a record. Supplies the nonrecord/extra-copy/personal-file exclusion tests and the competence-to-decide question, sourced to ISO 15489, RiC-CM and 36 CFR 1220.18.

decisions.concept: Record-to-record supersession (grok)
decisions.rationale: Base covers supersession only within one identity's version chain. Distinguishing a successor record from a new version, and denying that supersession authorises destruction, is an operative rule an agent needs and is DCMI-backed.

decisions.concept: Authoritative-record characteristics (grok)
decisions.rationale: Adds the ISO 15489/23081 authentic-reliable-integral-usable property set as dated assessed evidence, and repairs the base's weakest-evidenced area where ISO text was unavailable behind HTTP 403, using an accessible identical national adoption.

decisions.concept: Master and public identifiers (grok)
decisions.rationale: Base record-identity-anchor already carries scheme, granularity, non-reuse and alternate-identifier equivalence, and pins identity priority with DOI/ISO 26324 and MoReq2010 evidence. Grok adds no rule the base lacks.

decisions.concept: Descriptive metadata and classification assignment (grok)
decisions.rationale: Split across three base findings — designation-and-reference-numbers, documentary-form and classification-and-aggregation — which additionally add scheme versioning, reclassification history and multi-class precedence that Grok lacks.

decisions.concept: Fixity and extent (grok)
decisions.rationale: Base fixity-and-preservation-actions covers baseline digest, verification history, byte-changing actions and failure handling. Only declared-versus-measured extent is genuinely absent, and that is a question-level gap not worth importing a near-duplicate finding for; deferred instead.

decisions.concept: Record relationships / DCMI relation family (grok)
decisions.rationale: Part/whole, format-of, version-of, derivation and set membership are all already carried across base findings. Only requires/isRequiredBy dependency links are missing, so the residue is deferred as a question addition rather than importing overlapping structure.

decisions.concept: OAIS preservation package events / SIP-AIP-DIP (grok)
decisions.rationale: Base exchange-packaging-and-projections already treats a package as a projection of one record and demands reconstructability, and format-identification-and-environment covers rendering environment. OAIS ISO 14721:2025 is absent from base sources, so the alignment is deferred rather than the structure imported.

decisions.concept: C2PA content-credentials binding (grok)
decisions.rationale: Base already carries content-credential manifests as per-instantiation provenance evidence and records the hard-binding-cannot-be-identity resolution as an explicit conflict, which is the same rule Grok states.

decisions.concept: Legal and administrative holds (grok)
decisions.rationale: Base holds-and-suspension carries scope, authority, release condition and anti-automation enforcement with retrieved MoReq2010 text; Grok itself records that its hold schemas rest on partial primary support with DoD 5015.02 and MoReq unretrieved.

decisions.concept: Disposition execution and last-copy rule (grok)
decisions.disposition: rejected as a finding; gap retained
decisions.rationale: Base disposition-execution-and-evidence duplicates authorisation, method, survivors and transfer. The one distinctive rule — destroying one instantiation is not destroying the record while another authoritative instantiation remains — is an unresolved aggregate-scope gap and is deferred rather than imported inside a duplicate finding.

decisions.concept: Rights and licences (grok)
decisions.rationale: Base rights-licensing-and-personal-data covers rights holder, licence, personal-data lawful basis and redaction-as-derivative. The distinctive erasure-versus-retention conflict rests on GDPR text neither provider retrieved, so it is deferred rather than accepted.

decisions.concept: Certified copies and use events (grok)
decisions.rationale: Certified copies are covered by base instantiation-copy-and-original-status with its attestation artifact and fn-issue-certified-copy; use logging is covered by lifecycle-events-and-audit-trail and access decision recording.

decisions.concept: Archival aggregation (fonds, series, record sets)
decisions.rationale: Both providers independently exclude it on RiC grounds, keeping only membership references and the aggregate identifier at filing time. The agreement is treated as settled and the boundary is carried into the merged model unchanged.

decisions.concept: Grok-only operations: classify, register, migrate, assess
decisions.rationale: Each corresponds to a base finding that currently has no operation, so accepting them closes operating-surface gaps without introducing structure that competes with existing functions.

decisions.concept: Standards conformance language
decisions.rationale: Both providers normalise across three incompatible manifestation models (PREMIS, RiC, DCMI) and explicitly disclaim conformance; the merged draft must inherit that disclaimer rather than either provider's alignment wording.

publicationHolds: Source verification incomplete: re-verify every accepted source URL live and pin its version before publication. Claude's ISO 15489-1 source returned HTTP 403 and its ISO-attributed claims were read from catalogue abstracts and indexed extracts; re-verify them against Grok's JIS X 0902-1:2019 identical adoption or licensed ISO text before any ISO-derived statement is published.

eIDAS evidence is second-hand on both sides: Claude used the legislation.gov.uk rendition of Article 3 and flags that Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 amendments are not reflected; Grok used a European Commission FAQ guidance page. Re-pin signature, seal and qualified-timestamp tiers to consolidated EU text before publishing the assurance-tier vocabulary.

Instrument version drift must be reconciled to one pinned version each: RiC-O 1.1 (2025, Claude) versus RiC-CM 1.0 (2023, Grok), and C2PA 2.1 (Claude) versus C2PA 2.4 (Grok). Publish only after the record/instantiation split and the hard-binding rule are re-checked against the chosen versions.

Multi-profile domain validation not yet complete: the merged model has been reasoned mainly against archival and government recordkeeping profiles. Validate against at least three materially different profiles — an EU qualified-signature commercial instrument, a US federal case file under 36 CFR, and a media or generated-content asset carrying content credentials — before publication.
Confirm the WM-REC-015 boundary once that model exists, so aggregation-membership references and the record-set exclusion resolve to real structure rather than a placeholder neighbour.
Strip any residual conformance-claim wording inherited from either provider; the published draft must state alignment and mapping only, with lossiness recorded.
deferredResearch: Electronic transferable records under UNCITRAL MLETR: control, singularity and guaranteed uniqueness. Claude marks it a declared gap and Grok does not model it; likely a sibling model rather than an addition here.

Conflict-of-laws rule set for records created in one jurisdiction, held in a second and disclosed in a third. Both providers carry jurisdiction as a field with no sourced resolution rule; keep marked as a gap, never as canonical.

GDPR Article 17 erasure versus authorised retention duty: fetch the primary text and decide whether the conflict is carried as an unresolved question on the record or delegated to a rights/consent sibling model. Neither provider retrieved it.

Last-copy and multi-instantiation destruction semantics: when destruction of one instantiation does or does not destroy the record identity, and how the tombstone reflects partial destruction. Grok raises it; the base has no rule.

OAIS ISO 14721:2025 alignment: representation information for a designated community and SIP/AIP/DIP package roles — decide align-versus-reference against the base exchange-packaging finding rather than importing package structure.

Legal-hold primary schemas not retrieved by either provider: DoD 5015.02-STD, the MoReq2010 hold module in detail, and FRCP 37(e). Needed before hold scope, overlapping holds and release semantics can be stated as sourced rather than pattern-based.

Requires/isRequiredBy and references/isReferencedBy dependency relations between records (an annex, schema or referenced instrument needed to interpret the record) — evaluate as question-level additions to the content-and-components layer.
Declared-versus-measured extent (bytes, pages, duration) as a validation check on an instantiation; currently implied by the base coverage checklist but present in no base question.
InterPARES authenticity requirements and ISO 16175 / 14641 / 17068, none retrieved by either provider, as corroboration for the accepted authoritative-record-characteristics finding.

bundles.name: Identity, documentary form and classification
bundles.description: What the record is, how it is named and referenced, what documentary genre it belongs to, and where it sits in a business classification scheme and archival aggregation.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 treats classification and identification as the controls from which every later recordkeeping decision derives, and RiC-O separates the record from the sets that contain it; an agent cannot apply retention, access or authenticity rules before these are fixed.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: The stable identifier of the record as an information object and the human-facing titles and reference numbers layered on top of it.

findings.name: Record identity anchor
findings.description: The identifier that denotes the record independently of any file, version or rendition, its scheme, its granularity and its non-reuse guarantee.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifier values are inline reference data that must appear in every projection, including existence-level ones. The evidencing artifact for identifier assignment is the register entry produced under issuance and registration, so a separate artifact here would duplicate it.

findings.name: Designation and reference numbers
findings.description: Titles, alternative and translated titles, and the official reference numbers quoted on the face of the record, kept strictly distinct from identity.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Designation is descriptive inline metadata carried on the record; no separate artifact is produced by titling, and treating a title list as an artifact would invite its use as an identifier, which the identity rule forbids.

layers.name: Documentary form and classification
layers.description: The genre of the record and its placement in a business classification scheme and archival aggregation, which drive the rules that later apply to it.

findings.name: Documentary form and genre
findings.description: The documentary form the record takes (contract, certificate, invoice, minutes, licence) typed against a controlled vocabulary, and the rules that follow from that form.

findings.name: Business classification and aggregation membership
findings.description: Filing of the record under a classification class and its membership in aggregations, with the boundary to the archival aggregation model held explicitly.

bundles.name: Content, versions and manifestations
bundles.description: What the record says, the immutable states its content passes through, and the format-specific and carrier-specific realisations that make it readable.
bundles.rationale: PREMIS distinguishes Intellectual Entity, Representation, File and Bitstream, and RiC-O separates record resource from instantiation; collapsing these layers makes format migration indistinguishable from content change and destroys the evidentiary chain.

layers.name: Content and components
layers.description: The body of the record, its structural parts, attachments and the properties that must survive any transformation.

findings.name: Content structure, components and completeness
findings.description: Which parts make up the complete record, which are essential to its meaning, and how completeness is verified at capture.

layers.name: Versions and instantiations
layers.description: The immutable version chain of content states and the multiple physical or digital instantiations that realise each state.

findings.name: Version chain and immutability
findings.description: How a content state is fixed, how versions supersede and amend one another, and the prohibition on editing an issued version in place.

findings.name: Instantiation, copy and original status
findings.description: Format-specific and carrier-specific realisations of a version, and the legal distinction between the original of record, duplicates, certified copies and extracts.

findings.name: Supersession between records
findings.description: Dublin Core replaces/isReplacedBy model a related resource that supplants another. A new record may supersede an older record (policy, specification, licence) without being a version of the same identity. Supersession does not by itself authorize destruction of the replaced record; disposition remains a separate control.

layers.name: Format, fixity and preservation
layers.description: Technical identification of instantiations, the environment needed to render them, and the integrity and preservation controls applied over time.

findings.name: Format identification and rendering environment
findings.description: How each instantiation's format is identified against registries and what software and hardware environment is required to render it.

findings.name: Fixity and preservation actions
findings.description: Baseline digests, verification history, declared preservation level and the actions applied to keep instantiations readable, including those that change bytes.

bundles.name: Agency, authority and issuance
bundles.description: Who is responsible for the record, who owns and who keeps it, and the act of issuing it under a mandate and entering it into a register.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 makes assigned responsibility a precondition of trustworthy recordkeeping, RiC-O models Mandate and Agent as distinct contextual entities, and eIDAS makes the issuing legal person material to legal effect; ownership must be separable from custody.

layers.name: Agents, ownership and custody
layers.description: Role-qualified references to the agents who made, approved, own and keep the record.

findings.name: Authorship and responsibility roles
findings.description: Who authored, contributed to, approved and was addressed by the record, expressed as role-qualified references rather than embedded agent descriptions.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Agent attributes are governed by the person and organization models; this finding stores only role-qualified references, and the artifacts that evidence responsibility are the signature object and the event history recorded in other findings.

findings.name: Ownership, custody and stewardship
findings.description: The separation between the record owner and the custodian or registrar acting on the owner's behalf, and the terms limiting custodial power.

layers.name: Issuance and registration
layers.description: The act of issuing the record under a mandate in a jurisdiction, and its entry into a custodial or public register.

findings.name: Issuance, mandate and register entry
findings.description: The legal basis and jurisdiction under which the record was issued, and the register entry that anchors it in a custodial system.

bundles.name: Authenticity and evidentiary value
bundles.description: Why the record can be relied on: signatures and seals bound to fixed content, trusted timestamps, dated validation outcomes, derivation provenance and an unbroken chain of custody.
bundles.rationale: ISO 15489 makes authenticity and integrity defining characteristics of an authoritative record, eIDAS attaches legal effect to signature and timestamp tiers, and PROV-O and C2PA supply the derivation and binding structures; validity is time-dependent and must be recorded as evidence, not asserted as a flag.

layers.name: Signatures, seals and validation evidence
layers.description: Signature and seal objects bound to specific content, the timestamps that fix their moment, and the dated results of validating them.

findings.name: Signature, seal and attestation
findings.description: Signatures, seals and attestations applied to a version or instantiation, their assurance tier, their signatory and exactly what content each binds.

findings.name: Timestamping and validation evidence
findings.description: Trusted time-stamp tokens proving existence at a time, validation outcomes recorded with their own validation instant and policy, and the renewal of evidence before algorithms weaken.

findings.name: Authoritative record characteristics
findings.description: ISO 23081 states that metadata must support assertions of integrity, authenticity, reliability and usability over time in business context. ISO 15489 requires records to remain authoritative through those characteristics: authentic (what it purports to be, created or sent by the purported agent at the purported time), reliable (trusted full and accurate content of the transaction), integrity (complete and unaltered), usable (locatable, retrievable, presentable, interpretable). These are assessed properties with evidence, not decorative flags.

layers.name: Provenance and chain of custody
layers.description: Where the record came from and who held it at every moment between creation and now.

findings.name: Derivation and provenance graph
findings.description: The activities that generated the record, the sources it derives from, and the agents associated with each generating activity.

findings.name: Chain of custody and hand-over
findings.description: The gapless sequence of custody intervals, hand-over receipts and integrity checks that allows the record to be relied on as evidence.

bundles.name: State, time and recordkeeping control
bundles.description: The status the record is in, the events that moved it there, the time anchors it carries, and the retention, hold and disposition regime that decides its end.
bundles.rationale: NARA's universal requirements organise records systems by lifecycle from capture through disposal and transfer, MoReq2010 requires an event history on every entity and separates disposal scheduling from disposal holding, and RFC 3339 makes explicit offsets mandatory; state, time and disposition are one control problem.

layers.name: Status, lifecycle events and time
layers.description: Controlled status values, the append-only history of what happened, and the distinct time anchors the record carries.

findings.name: Record status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The controlled status vocabulary, which transitions are permitted from each state, who may authorise them, and how withdrawal differs from destruction.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is inline state carried directly on the record and required in every projection including existence-level views; its evidence is the event history artifact in the adjacent finding, so a duplicate artifact would be a second source of truth.

findings.name: Lifecycle events and audit trail
findings.description: The append-only history of everything done to and with the record, using controlled event types with actor, outcome, event time and separately recorded observation time.

findings.name: Temporal anchors and validity periods
findings.description: The distinct time anchors a record carries — created, issued, effective, expiry, received, observed — their precision, and the rule separating event time from ingestion time.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Time anchors are inline scalar values attached to the record, its versions and its events; the artifacts that carry temporal evidence are the trusted time-stamp token and the event history, both defined in other findings.

findings.name: Document versus captured record
findings.description: ISO 15489 applies to records regardless of structure or form and treats capture into a records system as the act that places identified information under records controls. RiC-CM defines a Record as discrete information content formed and inscribed, at least once, on any persistent recoverable carrier by an agent in the course of activity. US 36 CFR 1220.18 / 44 U.S.C. 3301 additionally excludes extra copies kept only for reference, library or museum materials for exhibit, and personal files. This model stores a record-status on the object: document-not-captured, captured-record, nonrecord-copy, or jurisdiction-specific Federal-record, rather than splitting into two meta-models.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and holds
layers.description: The authorised schedule that decides the record's fate, the suspensions that override it, and the evidence that survives execution.

findings.name: Retention class and disposition authority
findings.description: The retention class assigned to the record, the instrument authorising it, the trigger that starts the clock and the action due at the end.

findings.name: Holds and disposition suspension
findings.description: Legal holds and other suspensions that override retention schedules until explicitly released, and the mechanism that prevents automated disposal of held records.

findings.name: Disposition execution and surviving evidence
findings.description: Carrying out destruction, transfer or permanent retention, and the evidence and tombstone that outlive the record itself.

bundles.name: Access, rights and interoperability
bundles.description: Who may see what, on what legal footing content may be reused, and how the record and its evidence move between systems without losing meaning.
bundles.rationale: NARA's transfer guidance makes access restriction status a mandatory transfer element, DCMI supplies accessRights, license and rightsHolder, and IANA and format registries govern the value space for exchange; access and interoperability are governed together because every projection is an access decision.

layers.name: Access, security marking and rights
layers.description: Markings and decisions controlling who may read the record, and the intellectual-property and personal-data constraints on reuse.

findings.name: Access conditions and security marking
findings.description: The security marking and access restriction status carried by the record, the statutory regime behind them, and the recorded decisions on individual requests.

findings.name: Rights, licensing and personal data
findings.description: Who holds rights in the content, under what licence it may be reused, and what personal data within it constrains processing and release.

layers.name: Interoperability and exchange
layers.description: Declared mappings to external metadata standards and the packaging and projection rules for moving records between systems.

findings.name: Metadata alignment and conformance evidence
findings.description: Which external standards the record's metadata is mapped to, where mappings lose information, and what evidence is required before any conformance claim is made.

findings.name: Exchange packaging and projections
findings.description: How a record and its evidence are packaged for transfer or publication, and how each projection deliberately omits parts without breaking reconstructability.

model.name: Claim / Proposition
model.purpose: Provide a format-neutral record of a truth-apt assertion: what proposition is asserted, under what scope and qualification, by whom and with what standing, how it relates to other claims, which evidence and assessments it references, and how the claim record itself is identified, versioned, validated, restricted and disposed of. The model records assertion, not verdicts.
model.scope_statement: WM-KNW-007 covers the claim record as an object of knowledge management: propositional content and canonical form, identity and equivalence, scope and qualification (subject, place, time, conditions, measurand), stated calibrated uncertainty, the assertion act and asserting authority, provenance and ownership of the record, typed claim-to-claim relations, bound references to evidence and assessments, record lifecycle and versioning, well-formedness validation, sensitivity/access classification and disposition, and interoperability projections. It excludes the evidence items themselves, the appraisal of evidence bodies, the application and evaluation of inference schemes, the execution of fact-checking or verification, policy enforcement, and runtime audit trails owned by other systems.
in_scope: Canonical truth-apt statement, its language, atomicity and optional normalized subject-property-value or logical form
Claim identity, aliases, equivalence, restatement and translation relationships
Scope qualifiers: subject or population range, spatial extent, validity interval, conditions, assumptions, scenarios and known defeaters
Quantitative content of measurement claims: measurand, value, unit, stated coverage interval
Calibrated qualification stated on the claim: confidence and likelihood terms, scale reference and traceable-account pointer
The assertion act: claimant, role, illocutionary commitment, first and subsequent appearances, asserting authority and mandate
Provenance, attribution, derivation, ownership, stewardship and rights of the claim record
Typed claim-to-claim relations: entailment, specialization, contradiction, rebuttal, preference, supersession
Bound references to evidence items, external assessments/reviews and argument structures, carrying binding parameters only
Record lifecycle states, transitions, versioning, patch rules and externally issued retraction or correction references
Well-formedness shapes, required-field profiles and quality/testability signals for the record
Sensitivity classification, access policy expression, retention schedule, tombstones and disposition rules
Interoperability alignments and lossy-projection declarations across PROV-O, schema.org, VC 2.0, AIF, nanopublication and RDF 1.2
out_of_scope: Evidence items, citations, source descriptions, evidence typology, evidence appraisal and evidence lifecycle, which are owned by WM-KNW-008
Application and evaluation of inference, conflict and preference rules (AIF RA, CA and PA node semantics) and any defeasible-reasoning engine
Execution of fact-checking, verification or adjudication workflows, and the rating semantics, reviewer processes and audit trails of assessment systems
Runtime enforcement or evaluation of access and usage policies, and policy-decision logging
The real-world entities, events and quantities the claim is about, which belong to subject-domain models
Documents, publications and media that carry a claim, and publisher retraction workflows executed under NISO CREC
Cryptographic proof, credential status lists and verification procedures of Verifiable Credentials transport
Agent belief state, trust scoring of claimants or sources, and reputation computation
Storage engines, serializations and access interfaces (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB are projections)
Generic knowledge-asset register mechanics inherited from the parent model WM-KNW-001

boundary_notes.distinction: This model carries the evidence reference, the binding role (supports, challenges, qualifies), directionality and a locally stated binding weight. It never carries the evidence item's description, provenance, appraisal grade or lifecycle; those are dereferenced from WM-KNW-008 and are never copied into a claim record.

A claim corresponds to the AIF I-node level. Applications of rules of inference (RA), conflict (CA) and preference (PA), argument-scheme definitions and any evaluation of argument acceptability belong to an argumentation model. This model records only that a claim occupies a premise or conclusion role in an externally identified argument structure.

This model holds the reviewable claim and a reference to reviews of it. The review's rating scale, reviewer identity workflow, publication and audit trail are owned by the reviewing system; a review reference is never read as a truth value on the claim record.

PROV terms are used as alignment for attribution, derivation, revision and invalidation of the claim record. This model does not own generic Activity/Agent modelling, provenance-of-provenance bundles or provenance query semantics.

A VC claim is a subject-property-value assertion carried inside a credential secured by proof. This model treats the proposition independently of transport: credential validity, status and cryptographic verification are owned by credential models and must not be interpreted as claim truth or claim lifecycle.

A quantitative claim references a measurand, a value with unit and a stated coverage interval. The measurement procedure, instrument, calibration and metrological traceability chain belong to a measurement or observation model.

This model expresses sensitivity classes and ODRL policies about claim records. ODRL is a policy expression language that defines no enforcement or evaluation semantics, and none is claimed here; decisioning and its logs belong to the adopting Dimension's platform.

Generic knowledge-asset identity, register governance, stewardship and licensing are inherited through the CHILD link. This model specializes only what makes a record truth-apt: proposition, qualification, assertion and claim relations.

functions.name: Register claim
functions.description: Create a claim record in draft from an observed or reported assertion, capturing the canonical statement, language, claim type, claimant and the two distinct timestamps.
inputs: Candidate statement text with language tag
outputs: Draft claim record with assigned identifier
preconditions: Content passes the truth-aptness gate
Owning package and accountable steward are declared
A claim type from the scheme in force can be assigned
effects: Creates a new record in draft state
Records assertion time and ingestion time separately in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset
Creates no evidence, review or argument records

functions.name: Normalize claim statement
functions.description: Produce the canonical serialization and optional structured form of the statement so that equivalence comparison and digesting are deterministic.
inputs: Canonical statement text and language tag
outputs: Content digest as secondary equivalence key
preconditions: Language tag is present
Normalization profile is published and versioned
effects: Enables deterministic comparison across records
Does not alter the asserted meaning or the stored canonical text

functions.name: Assign claim identity
functions.description: Select and bind the record's primary identifier by identity priority, attaching aliases for identifiers issued by other systems.
preconditions: Identity priority is declared by the owning package
Namespace resolution commitment exists for the retention period
effects: Binds a stable identifier containing no date component
Replaces a locally minted identifier with an alias rather than a new record when a master identifier is later discovered

functions.name: Qualify claim scope
functions.description: Attach subject, population, spatial, temporal, condition and measurand qualifiers that bound the assertion, and flag scope that remains unresolved.
inputs: Measurand, value and unit where quantitative
preconditions: Claim type assigned so the required-field profile is known
effects: Narrows the record's applicability to the stated conditions
Raises promotion blockers where type-required qualifiers are missing

functions.name: State calibrated confidence
functions.description: Record the calibrated confidence or likelihood term the asserter attached, bound to a registered scale version, with a pointer to the traceable account that justifies it.
preconditions: The scale is registered and its version is in force
The traceable-account reference resolves
effects: Records a stated qualification only
Stores no evidence-body appraisal grade, which remains dereferenced from the evidence model

functions.name: Bind evidence reference
functions.description: Attach a qualified reference from the claim to an evidence item, carrying the binding role, directionality and locally stated weight and nothing else.
inputs: Evidence item identifier in the referenced evidence model
Directionality and locally stated binding weight
preconditions: Target identifier resolves
Role code exists in the registered code list
effects: Adds or updates a local edge only
Never writes to the evidence model and never copies evidence description, provenance or appraisal into the claim record

functions.name: Assert claim relation
functions.description: Record a typed relation between two claim records — entailment, specialization, presupposition, conflict, preference or supersession — with its ground and asserter.
preconditions: Both claim records exist
Relation code is registered
Supersession would not create a cycle
effects: Records the relation as a qualified edge
Registers conflict without resolving it and preference without applying it in any evaluation

functions.name: Transition claim status
functions.description: Move a claim record between permitted lifecycle states, setting effective and terminal timestamps and any successor reference.
inputs: Acting role, reason and effective instant
preconditions: The transition is permitted by the state scheme in force
The acting role is authorised for that transition
Promotion preconditions are satisfied when leaving draft
effects: Changes state and writes the transition record for this model's own record
Sets an invalidation timestamp and successor reference on terminal transitions

functions.name: Record status notice reference
functions.description: Attach a reference to an externally issued retraction, removal, correction or expression-of-concern notice and apply the declared local status effect.
inputs: Review determination where the effect is not automatic
outputs: Notice reference on the claim record
preconditions: The notice was issued by an authority outside this model
The notice type maps to a declared local status effect
effects: Records the reference and applies the local status effect
Does not issue, publish or propagate the notice, which remains the issuing publisher's or authority's responsibility

functions.name: Validate claim record
functions.description: Check a claim record against the published shapes package and the claim-type required-field profile, producing a severity-graded conformance report.
preconditions: Shapes package is published with a digest
The record's claim type is assigned
effects: Blocks promotion out of draft while violations remain
Owns shapes and profiles only; execution is performed by an external conformant validation processor whose engine and run logs are not owned here

functions.name: Classify sensitivity and express access conditions
functions.description: Assign a sensitivity class to a claim record and express the resulting permissions, prohibitions and duties as a declarative policy.
preconditions: Statement text has been reviewed for personal data and allegation content
Classifying role is authorised
effects: Records a class and a policy expression
Performs no evaluation, decisioning or enforcement, which belong to the adopting Dimension's platform

functions.name: Project claim record
functions.description: Emit a claim record in a target exchange profile using the crosswalk edition in force, declaring what the projection drops.
preconditions: A crosswalk edition covering the target profile exists
The assertion mode for graph projections has been determined
effects: Produces an exchange artifact marked with the crosswalk edition used
Marks a lossy projection as unusable as a record of identity and never converts an unasserted reifier into an asserted graph

functions.name: Dispose claim record
functions.description: Apply the disposition schedule to a terminated record, writing a tombstone, redacting statement text where an erasure obligation requires it, and notifying dependents.
preconditions: A terminal status has been reached or an erasure obligation has been established
Approving role has authorised any redaction
effects: Retains identifier, terminal status, terminal timestamp and successor reference in the tombstone
Never deletes referenced evidence, reviews or argument structures; removes only the local reference edge
Defines the rule only: execution across stores, indexes, caches and downstream copies is owned by the adopting Dimension

composition.purpose: Inherit generic knowledge-asset identity, register governance, stewardship and licensing from the parent so this model specializes only what makes a record truth-apt. The separation of an assertion from the record metadata about it, as in PROV and the nanopublication pattern, is what makes this inheritance clean rather than duplicative.

Carry the evidence item identifier, binding role, directionality and a locally stated binding weight so a claim can be shown as supported or challenged. Evidence description, provenance, appraisal grades and evidence lifecycle remain owned by the target and are dereferenced, never copied.

composition.target: W3C PROV-O (prov:Entity, wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, hadPrimarySource, wasRevisionOf, invalidatedAtTime, prov:Bundle)
composition.purpose: Express record attribution, derivation, primary source, revision and invalidation using established provenance terms. Generic Activity and Agent modelling and provenance query semantics remain with PROV; this is alignment, not a conformance claim.

Map canonical statement text, appearance and firstAppearance, and express reviews of a claim as external ClaimReview references. schema.org defines no formal claim-to-claim relations, so the model's typed relation layer is additional and must be declared as such in the crosswalk.

composition.target: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 claim (subject-property-value)
composition.purpose: Align the normalized statement form with the VC subject-property-value structure so claims can be carried in credentials. Issuer proof, credentialStatus and validity windows belong to credential transport and must never be read as claim truth or claim lifecycle.

Map a claim record to the AIF I-node level so claims can participate in argument graphs. Applications of rules of inference, conflict and preference (RA, CA, PA) and schematic form nodes stay with the argumentation model.

composition.target: Nanopublication head / assertion / provenance / publicationInfo graph pattern
composition.purpose: Adopt the separation of the minimal assertion from its provenance and publication metadata as the reference projection for graph exchange, and adopt the guidance to keep assertions minimal as the basis of the atomicity rule.

composition.target: W3C RDF 1.2 triple terms, reifying triples and named graphs
composition.purpose: Provide statement-level identity in graph projections and preserve the distinction between naming a statement and asserting it, so that an unasserted reifier is never silently promoted to an asserted assertion graph.

composition.target: W3C SHACL shapes and validation reports
composition.purpose: Publish the model's shapes and required-field profiles for execution by any conformant processor. Validation execution, processor failures and run logs are owned by the processor and its operator, not by this model.

Express permissions, prohibitions, duties and constraints over claim records declaratively. ODRL defines no enforcement or evaluation mechanism, so no decisioning, enforcement or policy-decision logging is claimed here.

composition.target: IPCC calibrated uncertainty language (evidence and agreement, confidence and likelihood scales)
composition.purpose: Bind the stated confidence and likelihood terms on a claim to a published calibrated scale with a traceable account, and adopt the requirement to specify variables, region, period and conditions as the basis of the scope-qualifier layer.

composition.target: JCGM 200:2012 VIM (measurand, measurement uncertainty, coverage interval, metrological traceability)
composition.purpose: Use agreed metrology terms for the quantitative content of measurement claims. Measurement procedure, calibration and the metrological traceability chain remain with a metrology or observation model.

composition.target: NISO RP-45-2024 CREC retraction, removal and expression-of-concern metadata
composition.purpose: Align the shape of externally issued status-notice references and the requirement that an affected item's status be visible to readers. Issuance, publication and propagation of notices stay with publishers, aggregators and hosts.
Constrain every time value in the model to a date-time with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and preserve the RFC's distinction between an unknown local offset and UTC.

composition.target: FAIR Guiding Principles F1, I3 and R1.2
composition.purpose: Require globally unique persistent identifiers for claim records, qualified rather than bare references for claim relations and evidence bindings, and detailed record provenance.

composition.target: Argumentation / inference-scheme model (not yet registered - declared gap)
composition.purpose: Placeholder for the sibling that must own argument-scheme definition, inference, conflict and preference rule application and any evaluation of argument acceptability. Until it is registered this remains a declared gap; no local ownership of those semantics is asserted and only a role reference is held.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension MUST name one owning package for the claim register and one accountable claim steward before any record is promoted out of draft; an unowned register may hold drafts only.
The owning package MUST declare which authority's identifiers are treated as master for its claim population, and MUST NOT mint local UUIDs or ULIDs where a master identifier already exists.

The owning package MUST publish and version its claim-type scheme, its calibrated uncertainty scale binding, its lifecycle state scheme and its shapes package; records created under a superseded version remain valid and are migrated by explicit patch, never by silent reinterpretation.

The owning package MUST NOT store evidence descriptions, evidence appraisal grades, review ratings or argument-scheme definitions locally; it stores resolvable references and the binding parameters this model owns.
The owning package MUST declare the enforcement platform that evaluates its access policies and the party that executes disposition, since this model owns neither.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Claim identifiers live under a namespace the owning package controls and can keep resolvable for the record's full retention period. An identifier MUST NOT be reused for a different proposition, MUST NOT encode status, confidence, claim type or any date component, and MUST survive restatement and translation of the claim text. Alignment namespaces for provenance, schema, argumentation, nanopublication, shapes and policy vocabularies are imported as external terms and are never re-minted or shadowed under the local namespace; where a local term is needed because no external term exists, it is minted locally and declared in the crosswalk as an extension rather than presented as a standard term.
registry_links: vr.wm-knw-007 is the registry entry of record for this model, at nav path NAV.INF.KNW.CLM under domain tags INF.KNW.CLM.
WM-KNW-001 is the registered parent and supplies generic knowledge-asset governance through the CHILD link.
WM-KNW-008 is the registered REFERENCE target for evidence and citations; the relation ledger at planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv is authoritative and no local structure may contradict it.
The argumentation / inference-scheme owner is unregistered; the gap MUST be raised against the registry before any inference-scheme content is added anywhere in this model.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize statement text by trimming leading and trailing whitespace, collapsing internal runs of whitespace and normalizing Unicode to NFC, while preserving case, punctuation, diacritics and the language tag; do not lowercase, stem or strip stop words, because negation, named entities and hedges are meaning-bearing.

Canonicalize order-insensitive collections (claim relations, evidence bindings, alignments, appearance locators) by sorting on target identifier then relation or role code, so serialization order can never change a record digest.

Canonicalize all time values to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; retain the original offset rather than converting to UTC, because the offset carries assertion-context meaning, and preserve the distinction between an unknown local offset and UTC.

Treat unknown, empty and not-applicable as distinct: omit the field when a value is unknown, use the scheme's explicit not-applicable code where one exists, and never write a placeholder string such as 'n/a' or 'unknown' into a value field.
Canonicalize references as identifier plus relation qualifier; a bare identifier without its qualifier is not canonical and fails validation.
patch_rules: The canonical statement text of a record in asserted state is immutable: a change of meaning creates a new claim record linked by supersedes, while a typographic correction is a version patch that keeps the identifier and retains the prior text in the version manifest.

Patches are expressed as field-level operations against the canonical form with a precondition naming the prior version identifier; blind whole-document replacement and patches without a version precondition are rejected.

Adding, changing or removing an evidence binding, an assessment reference, a claim relation or a calibrated confidence value patches this record only and never writes into the evidence model, the reviewing system or the argumentation owner.
A patch that would alter scope qualifiers in a way that changes which subjects, places, periods or conditions the claim covers is a meaning change and follows the new-record rule, not the patch rule.
Every patch increments the version identifier and records actor, reason and RFC 3339 timestamp with offset.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional field, a new relation code, a new claim-type concept or a new alignment is backward compatible; narrowing cardinality, adding a required field, or retiring a claim-type, status or confidence-scale term is breaking and requires a new major profile version.
Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields and MUST NOT infer that a property is absent from the record merely because a projection profile does not carry it.

A projection that cannot carry the primary identifier, the canonical statement, the record status and the scope qualifiers MUST be declared lossy in the crosswalk and MUST NOT be used as a system of record.
Deprecated scheme terms remain resolvable with a successor pointer for at least the longest retention period of any record that used them.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the claim population, such as a standards-body clause or provision identifier, a regulator's decision reference, a registry claim number or a publisher-assigned claim key.
Governed global identifier or IRI, such as a persistent HTTP IRI under a controlled namespace, a DOI, or a content-derived global name issued by a governed publication network.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when no master or governed global identifier exists, and replaced by an alias rather than a new record if one is later discovered.

Content digest over the canonical normalized statement, permitted only as a secondary equivalence key and never as the record's primary identifier, because one proposition may have several texts and one text may express different claims in different contexts.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every time value in this model is an RFC 3339 date-time that includes seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; an unknown local offset is written as -00:00 and is not equivalent to Z. Event time and observation time are recorded separately and are never conflated: the assertion time (when the claimant asserted the proposition) and the claim's validity interval (the period for which the content is asserted true) are distinct from the ingestion or observation time (when this register captured the claim) and from the status effective time (when a lifecycle transition took effect). A date value alone is never an identifier and never a substitute for a timestamp where an instant is required.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts - claim-type scheme, uncertainty scale registry, lifecycle state scheme, shapes package, alignment crosswalk, stewardship declaration, disposition schedule and AGENTS.md - are named as owning-package, artifact slug and a monotonically increasing major.minor.patch sequence. The sequence never encodes a date or a status, is never reset, and a superseded serial is retained and marked superseded with a successor pointer rather than renamed, reused or deleted.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a named-algorithm content digest computed over its canonical serialization together with the identifier of the record set it governs. A claim record cites both the artifact serial and its digest; a digest mismatch invalidates the citation and blocks promotion rather than silently resolving to the current artifact version. Provenance bundles and version manifests are append-only, so integrity failures surface as an added correcting entry, never as an in-place rewrite.

policies: Assert-what-is-asserted: the register records that a proposition was asserted, by whom, under what qualification and with what standing. It never records this model's own view of the proposition's truth, and no field - not confidence, not authority standing, not a review reference, not a credential status - may be read or projected as a truth verdict.

Reference-not-replicate: evidence, citations, reviews, argument schemes, mandates, retraction notices and enforcement decisions are referenced by resolvable identifier. Only the binding parameters this model owns may be stored locally, and any field that begins to describe a referenced object is a boundary violation to be migrated to the owning model.
One record, one proposition: compound or composite statements are split before promotion, and a record failing the atomicity test cannot leave draft.

No silent reinterpretation: changing a scheme, scale, state model or shapes version never retroactively changes the meaning or conformance of existing records; migration is explicit, versioned and recorded.

Separation of expression from execution: this model expresses shapes, policies, disposition rules and status effects; validation processors, enforcement platforms, publishers and storage operators execute them and own their run logs.

read: Reading a claim record returns the primary identifier, canonical statement, language, claim type, scope qualifiers, stated confidence and status; evidence, review and argument information is returned as resolvable references, never as embedded copies.

Reads MUST support filtering and must always expose status, so that consumers cannot surface retracted, withdrawn or superseded claims as current; a projection that omits status is non-conforming and may not be used as a system of record.
Reading a superseded record returns its successor reference and reading a superseding record returns what it supersedes, so revision chains are traversable in both directions.
Reading a record whose statement text is withheld under sensitivity rules still returns identifier, claim type, status and the fact of withholding, so downstream copies remain reconcilable.
create: A claim record may be created only with a canonical statement, a language tag, a truth-aptness verdict, a claim type, a claimant reference or an explicit claimant-unknown code, an assertion timestamp or explicit unknown-time code, and an owning package with an accountable steward.

Identity is assigned at creation in identity-priority order; a locally minted identifier discovered later to have a master equivalent is superseded by an alias binding, not by creating a second record.
Creation records ingestion or observation time separately from assertion time, both as RFC 3339 values with seconds and an offset.
Creation never creates records in referenced models; an evidence item or review that does not yet exist is raised with its owner rather than stubbed locally.
update: Scope qualifiers, calibrated confidence, relations, bindings, alignments and sensitivity classification are updatable in place under the patch rules, each update incrementing the version identifier and recording actor, reason and timestamp.
Status changes are performed only through the status transition function and are constrained by the lifecycle state scheme in force; a direct write to the status field is rejected.
The canonical statement of an asserted record is not updatable in meaning; meaning changes create a new record linked by supersedes.
Updates never mutate a referenced model's records; a needed change to evidence, a review or an argument structure is raised as a request to that model's owner and tracked as an open referral.
delete: Default is non-destructive: an asserted claim record is never physically removed. It is transitioned to a terminal status, keeps its primary identifier, and retains a tombstone carrying the identifier, terminal status, terminal timestamp, redaction marker where applicable and successor reference where superseded.

Hard deletion is permitted only for records never published outside the owning package, or where an erasure obligation applies to personal data embedded in the statement; in that case the statement text is redacted while the identifier, claim type, status and tombstone survive so downstream copies remain reconcilable.

Retention periods and disposition triggers are bound to sensitivity class and terminal status by the disposition schedule; the schedule serial applied is recorded on the disposed record, and provenance bundles and version manifests inherit the record's retention rather than being purged independently.

This model owns the disposition rule and the tombstone shape only. Execution of erasure across stores, indexes, caches, backups and downstream copies is owned by the adopting Dimension's data-protection and storage policy; issuance and propagation of retraction or removal notices in publishing channels is owned by the issuing publisher, aggregator or authority under NISO CREC practice; deletion of referenced evidence records is owned by WM-KNW-008 and deletion of review records by the reviewing system.

Deleting or disposing of a claim record never deletes referenced evidence, reviews or argument structures; only the local reference edge is removed, and dependent claims holding relations to the disposed record are notified so their edges are marked dangling rather than silently broken.

roles.name: Claim Steward
responsibilities: Curate canonical statements and enforce the one-record-one-proposition rule
Assign claim type and populate the scope qualifiers the type requires
Promote records out of draft only when validation and quality gates pass
Record restatement, translation and equivalence links with the test applied

roles.name: Assertion Registrar
responsibilities: Record claimant identity, capacity, commitment level and appearance locators accurately
Record asserting authority, mandate reference and standing without treating standing as truth
Maintain the separation between assertion time, validity interval and ingestion time
Correct attribution errors promptly and record the correction

roles.name: Register Owner and Model Governor
responsibilities: Own the claim-type scheme, uncertainty scale registry, lifecycle state scheme, shapes package and crosswalk, including their serials and digests
Approve breaking profile changes and publish migration instructions
Adjudicate whether a change is a patch or a new claim when stewards disagree
Maintain the referenced-model contracts and raise boundary violations to the registry

roles.name: Data Protection and Access Officer
responsibilities: Classify sensitivity for records naming identifiable persons, unproven allegations and embargoed findings
Express access and use conditions as declarative policy and keep them current
Own the disposition schedule and approve any redaction of statement text
Delegate evaluation and enforcement to the adopting Dimension's platform and confirm execution of disposition

roles.name: Interoperability Engineer
responsibilities: Maintain crosswalk editions and declare per-profile lossiness
Determine the assertion mode for graph projections and guard against promoting an unasserted reifier to an asserted graph
Monitor upstream standard changes and record newly discovered inter-standard conflicts
Maintain the minimum interchange profile and the AGENTS.md bootstrap contract

access.default_rule: Claim records are readable to the owning package and to consumers granted the register's read scope, with status always exposed. A record whose statement names or renders identifiable a natural person and whose content is an unverified allegation defaults to restricted read until a sensitivity class has been assigned; write access to statement text, status and sensitivity class is restricted to the roles named in the stewardship declaration.
exceptions: Embargoed claims, such as pre-publication findings or matters under legal restriction, are withheld from general read until the embargo expiry instant, stored in RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, and the party responsible for confirming the lift is named.

Records containing special-category personal data or unproven allegations may have their canonical statement text withheld while identifier, claim type, status and the fact of withholding remain readable.

Retracted, withdrawn and superseded claims remain readable with a mandatory status indication; suppressing them entirely is prohibited because downstream copies must remain reconcilable with the register.
Break-glass read for legal, safety or regulatory review is permitted with a recorded reason, a named approver and a time limit set by the adopting Dimension.
Artifact-scope access may be granted independently of record-scope access, since schemes, scales, shapes and crosswalks are usually publishable even where individual claim records are restricted.
audit_requirements: Every status transition, statement patch, sensitivity reclassification, relation or binding change and disposition action on this model's own records is recorded with actor, reason, prior version and an RFC 3339 timestamp with offset in the model's version manifest and provenance bundle.

This model does not own runtime access logs, policy-decision logs, validation processor run logs or fact-check workflow trails; those are produced, retained and disposed of by the adopting Dimension's enforcement platform, the validation processor operator and the reviewing systems referenced from this model.

Audit entries in the version manifest and provenance bundle are append-only and inherit the retention of the record they describe; they are tombstoned rather than deleted, and a correction is added as a new entry rather than by rewriting an existing one.
Break-glass reads and redaction approvals are recorded with approver identity and expiry, and are reviewed by the Data Protection and Access Officer on the cycle the adopting Dimension declares.

required_fields: Scheme, scale, state model and shapes package serials in force
Referenced models and what each owns, including the prohibition on copying evidence, review or argument content locally
Minimum interchange profile and declared lossy projections
read_order: AGENTS.md at the package root, before any read or write operation is attempted
Specification URL, for scope, in-scope and out-of-scope lists and boundary notes, so that ownership limits are known before data is touched
Storage type URL, for the canonical form and the projection in use, since storage is a projection and not the semantics
Interface URL, for read and write operations, status filtering and the version-precondition requirement on patches
Processes URL, for registration, scope qualification, status transition, validation, projection and disposition procedures
Referenced-model contracts for WM-KNW-001 and WM-KNW-008, and the declared argumentation gap, before dereferencing any evidence, review or argument identifier

coverage.claim: Single-provider Claude draft for WM-KNW-007 covering the claim record as a governed knowledge object: canonical statement and logical form, identity and equivalence, subject/spatial/temporal/conditional scope, quantified content and calibrated uncertainty, the assertion act and asserting authority, record provenance, ownership and rights, typed claim-to-claim relations, qualified bindings to evidence, reviews and argument structures, lifecycle, versioning and externally issued notices, validation shapes, sensitivity, access and disposition, and interoperability projections — 6 bundles, 12 layers, 28 findings, 112 questions, 12 artifacts and 13 functions grounded in 14 declared sources. Two checklist dimensions remain open gaps (argument/inference ownership; privacy legal basis), several typologies are uncited design proposals, three findings have no operational function, and no independent second-provider review exists. No universal, domain-complete or metaphysical completeness is claimed.

checklist.notes: Identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed global identifier or IRI, then a locally minted UUID/ULID, with content digests demoted to a secondary equivalence key. No identifier may contain a date, status or confidence component. Grounded in RDF 1.2 IRI identity, FAIR F1 and nanopublication practice (SRC-009, SRC-014, SRC-006).

A published state scheme defines permitted states, transitions, authorised roles, promotion preconditions and terminal effects, with PROV invalidation semantics for termination and an explicit new-claim versus new-version rule. Externally issued retraction and correction notices are referenced, not issued here (SRC-001, SRC-012).

Entailment, specialization, presupposition, conflict, preference and supersession are recorded as qualified typed edges, matching the registry's TYPED-EDGES default. Registration is explicitly not adjudication: conflict resolution and preference application belong to the argumentation model (SRC-005, SRC-001, SRC-014).

Assertion time, validity interval, ingestion/observation time and status effective time are modelled as distinct values, all RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, with the unknown-local-offset case preserved as -00:00 (SRC-007, SRC-010).

Derivation, quotation, primary source, revision, generating agent and extraction method are captured, with extraction confidence kept distinct from the claim's own stated confidence, and materialised as an append-only provenance bundle following PROV and the nanopublication provenance graph (SRC-001, SRC-006).

Owning package, accountable steward, role-to-field write matrix, licence and rights for quoted text, and a succession rule on package retirement are declared in a serialised stewardship declaration (SRC-014, SRC-013).

A published shapes package with severity-graded constraints and per-claim-type required-field profiles gates promotion out of draft. The model owns shapes and profiles; execution is delegated to an external conformant processor whose engine and run logs are outside the boundary (SRC-008).

Sensitivity classes, a restricted default for unverified claims naming identifiable persons, embargo handling, break-glass exceptions and declarative policy expression are defined. ODRL is used for expression only; it defines no enforcement mechanism and none is claimed (SRC-013, SRC-002).

Non-destructive default with mandatory tombstone fields, narrow redaction conditions for embedded personal data, a serialised disposition schedule, and an explicit statement that this model owns the rule while the adopting Dimension executes erasure, publishers execute notices and referenced models own deletion of their own records (SRC-001, SRC-012, SRC-013).

A serialised crosswalk maps fields to PROV-O, schema.org, VC 2.0, AIF, nanopublication and RDF 1.2 with per-profile lossiness declarations, an explicit asserted-versus-reified projection decision, and recorded inter-standard conflicts. Alignment is never presented as conformance (SRC-002, SRC-003, SRC-004, SRC-005, SRC-006, SRC-009).

A truth-aptness gate rejects questions, commands, performatives and bare preferences, and a governed claim-type scheme drives type-specific required fields. Grounded in schema.org's factually oriented Claim definition and the IPCC requirement to specify what is being assessed (SRC-002, SRC-010).

Subject and population range with inclusion/exclusion criteria and aggregation level, spatial and jurisdictional extent, validity interval, scenario, assumptions and acknowledged defeaters are all modelled, following the IPCC instruction to specify variables, region, period and conditions (SRC-010).

Measurand, value, unit, stated coverage interval with coverage probability and comparator baseline are modelled, alongside a registered calibrated confidence and likelihood scale with a traceable-account pointer. Measurement procedure and traceability chains are out of scope (SRC-011, SRC-010).

Mandate reference, recognised jurisdiction and official/advisory/unofficial standing are recorded, with an explicit constraint preventing standing from being projected as a truth verdict. Mandates themselves remain instruments of their granting bodies (SRC-004, SRC-002, SRC-010).

Only target identifier, binding role, directionality, locally stated weight and binding status are held. Evidence description, provenance and appraisal grades are explicitly excluded, and a dedicated question tests for appraisal fields leaking into the calibrated-confidence finding (SRC-005, SRC-006, SRC-014).

No sibling model owning argument-scheme definition, inference/conflict/preference rule application or argument evaluation is registered. The model holds only an AIF I-node role reference and a declared placeholder composition link. Until that owner exists, any consumer wanting evaluated arguments has no in-registry target, and this node is marked a gap rather than presented as canonical (SRC-005).

Sensitivity classification, restricted defaults and redaction procedures are defined, but the underlying legal duties (accuracy, rectification, erasure) could not be cited from a retrievable primary legal source because the EUR-Lex client requests were blocked. This dimension rests on a regional assumption rather than a cited requirement and must be confirmed by the adopting Dimension's counsel.

known_omissions: The IPCC uncertainty guidance note (SRC-010) was read from a mirrored copy because the canonical ipcc.ch URL returned HTTP 403 to the research client; the cited URL is the canonical location and the content was verified against the mirror.

The JCGM 200:2012 PDF did not extract cleanly; VIM term coverage (measurand, measurement result, measurement uncertainty, coverage interval, coverage probability, metrological traceability) was confirmed from the BIPM catalogue description rather than full-text extraction, so the metrology link is declared an alignment and not a conformance claim.
EUR-Lex requests for Regulation (EU) 2016/679 were blocked, so data-protection duties are recorded as regional assumptions rather than cited requirements; no GDPR source is cited.

No normative registry of claim-to-claim relation types was found. The proposed relation codes synthesise AIF conflict and preference semantics with PROV revision semantics and are a design proposal, not a standard.

The commitment-level and illocutionary-force typology in the assertion-act finding has no cited normative source and is a design proposal drawing on the schema.org distinction between a claim and its review context.

Deontic and normative claims (obligations, permissions, recommendations) are covered only by the modality field; a full normative-statement model, including the relation between a norm and its enforcement, is not attempted here and ODRL is cited for policy about records rather than for norms as claim content.

Thresholds for cross-language claim equivalence, and any automated similarity method for deciding sameness, are left to the adopting Dimension; only the requirement to record the test applied is specified.
Aggregation of many claims into positions, consensus statements or knowledge-base states is not modelled; it would require the unregistered argumentation owner or a separate aggregate model.

The AIF specification PDF returned an imprecise automated summary on first extraction; RA, CA and PA node meanings were re-verified as applications of rules of inference, conflict and preference before use.
conflicts: schema.org models a Claim as a CreativeWork with text, name and appearance properties and defines no formal claim-to-claim relations, while AIF models the same content as an I-node inside a typed argument graph. A creative work and a proposition are different identity bearers, so the crosswalk must state which is the record of identity for a given exchange; this model treats the proposition as the identity bearer.

W3C VC 2.0 uses 'claim' for a subject-property-value assertion inside a credential whose standing depends on issuer, proof, validity window and credentialStatus, whereas this model treats a claim as truth-apt content independent of transport. Credential expiry, revocation or status MUST NOT be projected as claim falsity or as a claim lifecycle transition.

Nanopublication practice treats the assertion as minimal, immutable and content-addressed, whereas ClaimReview workflows expect claimReviewed to be an editable summary of prose. The model resolves this by making asserted statement meaning immutable and treating reviewer or curator summaries as separate restatement records rather than edits.

IPCC calibrated confidence is a property of an assessed finding derived from an appraised evidence body, while evidence-body certainty ratings sit on the evidence itself. Placing a confidence term on a claim without a resolvable traceable account risks double-counting appraisal that WM-KNW-008 owns; the model therefore stores the term and the pointer but forbids storing appraisal grades.

RDF 1.2 reifying triples allow a statement to be named and described without being asserted, whereas a nanopublication assertion graph is asserted by virtue of publication. A projection that converts a reifier into an assertion graph silently changes the record's assertive force and is prohibited.

NISO CREC assumes a scholarly publishing chain of publishers, aggregators and hosts, while claims in this register may originate from speech, regulation or data pipelines where no such chain exists. Where no issuer of notices exists, the model has no external source of retraction and must rely on its own status transitions, which is a weaker guarantee and must be declared.
regional_assumptions: EU/EEA: accuracy, rectification and erasure duties over personal data embedded in claim statements are assumed to apply, and the redaction and tombstone rules are designed to accommodate them; the legal text could not be retrieved by the research client and this is therefore an assumption, not a cited requirement.

Defamation and unproven-allegation exposure varies materially by jurisdiction. The restricted-read default for unverified claims naming identifiable persons is a conservative design choice, not a cited legal requirement, and the adopting Dimension must confirm it against local law.

NISO CREC is a US-originating recommended practice with international participation and is oriented to scholarly publishing; adoption by non-scholarly publishers, regulators or media organisations is not assumed.

IPCC calibrated language is authoritative within climate assessment. Reusing its confidence and likelihood scales in other domains is an alignment choice the adopting Dimension must declare explicitly, since the probability ranges carry assessment-specific conventions.

Canonical statements are assumed to carry a BCP 47 language tag. Normalization behaviour for right-to-left scripts, non-Latin scripts and languages without whitespace word boundaries is left to the adopting Dimension, and the NFC rule may need supplementing there.

Identifier namespace persistence assumes the owning package can maintain resolution for the full retention period; in jurisdictions or organisations without that capability, a governed external identifier authority should be used instead of local minting.
adversarial_checks: Boundary test against WM-KNW-008: every bundle, layer, finding, data element and function was re-read for evidence description, source appraisal, citation formatting or evidence lifecycle content.
