bundles.name: Proposition Content and Identity
bundles.description: What proposition the record asserts, in what form, of what kind, and how that proposition is identified and recognised as the same claim across restatements, translations and systems.
bundles.rationale: Nothing else in the model is well defined until the asserted proposition is fixed as a single truth-apt statement with a stable identifier. Schema.org locates claim content in text/name/sameAs, VC 2.0 fixes a subject-property-value structure, the nanopublication guidelines require minimal precisely defined assertions, and RDF 1.2 supplies IRI and statement-level identity.

layers.name: Content and Form
layers.description: The canonical statement, its logical shape and its type, including the test that decides whether the content is truth-apt at all.

findings.name: Canonical Statement
findings.description: The single declarative sentence the record asserts, held in a canonical surface form with a language tag, an optional normalized structured form for machine comparison, and an atomicity rule of one record to one proposition.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The canonical statement and its normalized form are the record's own primary field values, not a separately managed deliverable; the nanopublication guidance to keep assertions minimal implies inline triples rather than a document, and treating the statement as an artifact would create a second identity for the same proposition.

findings.name: Logical Form and Modality
findings.description: The structural properties that change what the statement asserts: polarity, quantification over the subject range, alethic or deontic modality, tense, and hedging that weakens the assertion.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Polarity, quantification, modality and hedges are coded attributes of the statement itself. Externalizing them into an artifact would separate them from the sentence whose meaning they determine and would allow the two to drift apart under patching.

findings.name: Claim Type and Truth-Aptness
findings.description: The gate test that admits only truth-apt content to the register, and the classification of admitted claims by the kind of proposition asserted, which drives which scope and qualification fields are required.

layers.name: Identity and Equivalence
layers.description: How a claim record is named, how aliases are held, and when two differently worded records are treated as the same proposition.

findings.name: Claim Identifier
findings.description: Assignment and resolution of the identifier that names this claim record, following the model's identity priority, with aliases for identifiers issued elsewhere and content digests kept only as secondary keys.

findings.name: Equivalence, Restatement and Translation
findings.description: The rules and recorded links that decide when a differently worded, summarised or translated statement is the same proposition, a restatement of it, or a genuinely different claim.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Equivalence, restatement and translation are qualified reference edges between existing records. Materialising them as a separate artifact would duplicate identity state that the identifier register already holds and would risk the artifact and the edges disagreeing.

bundles.name: Scope, Qualification and Stated Uncertainty
bundles.description: The conditions under which the claim is asserted to hold: over what subjects, where, when, under what assumptions, with what measured content, and with what calibrated confidence the asserter attached to it.
bundles.rationale: The IPCC guidance requires a finding to specify its variables, region, time period and conditions, and to carry calibrated confidence and likelihood terms backed by a traceable account; JCGM 200 supplies the agreed terms for measurands and stated uncertainty. Without these, a claim is untestable and comparisons between claims are unsound.

layers.name: Scope Qualifiers
layers.description: Subject range, spatial and temporal extent, and the conditions, assumptions and known defeaters that bound the assertion.

findings.name: Subject and Population Scope
findings.description: The entities the claim ranges over: the named subject or the population definition with inclusion and exclusion criteria, and the level of aggregation at which the claim is asserted.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject and population scope are per-claim field values and references to subject-domain identifiers. Publishing them as an artifact would either duplicate the domain model's entity descriptions or create a parallel population registry this model has no mandate to own.

findings.name: Spatial and Temporal Scope
findings.description: Where and for what period the claim is asserted to hold, kept strictly separate from when it was asserted and when the record was captured.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are timestamp and reference fields on the record. Their governance value comes from being adjacent to the statement they qualify; an artifact would add an indirection that makes the crucial event-time versus ingestion-time distinction easier to lose in projection.

findings.name: Conditions, Assumptions and Known Defeaters
findings.description: The scenario, background assumptions, ceteris paribus conditions and explicitly acknowledged defeating circumstances under which the claim is or is not asserted to hold.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Conditions and defeaters qualify one specific claim and are meaningless detached from it. Recording a defeater is a note that a defeating circumstance is acknowledged; evaluating whether it actually defeats the claim belongs to an argumentation model, so no local artifact should imply that adjudication happened here.

layers.name: Quantified Content and Calibrated Uncertainty
layers.description: Measured content of quantitative claims and the calibrated confidence or likelihood term the asserter attached, with the traceable account that justifies it held elsewhere.

findings.name: Quantitative Content and Measurand
findings.description: For claims asserting a quantity: the measurand as defined, the value and unit, the stated uncertainty as a coverage interval with its coverage probability, and the comparison basis where the claim is comparative.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Value, unit and stated interval are per-claim fields. The measurement procedure, calibration and metrological traceability chain that would justify an artifact belong to a metrology or observation model, so producing one here would assert ownership of measurement semantics this model explicitly disclaims.

findings.name: Calibrated Confidence and Likelihood
findings.description: The calibrated qualification the asserter attached to the claim, expressed with a registered scale term, plus the pointer to the traceable account that justifies it. The appraisal of the underlying evidence body is not held here.

bundles.name: Assertion, Provenance and Ownership
bundles.description: Who asserted the claim and with what standing, how the claim record came to exist, and who is accountable for it.
bundles.rationale: PROV-O supplies attribution, derivation, primary-source and revision terms; the nanopublication pattern separates assertion metadata from record metadata; VC 2.0 fixes the issuer as the party asserting claims; FAIR R1.2 requires detailed provenance. Together these ground both the assertion act and the record's own lineage and stewardship.

layers.name: Assertion Acts and Standing
layers.description: The act of asserting: claimant, commitment, appearance context, and whether the claimant held authority to assert.

findings.name: Claimant and Assertion Act
findings.description: Who asserted the proposition, in what capacity and with what degree of commitment, together with the first and subsequent contexts in which the assertion appeared.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The assertion act is captured as references to agents and to appearance locations in documents owned by content and publication models. Creating an artifact here would duplicate those documents and would blur the line between recording that an assertion occurred and republishing the material that carried it.

findings.name: Asserting Authority and Mandate
findings.description: Whether the claimant held a recognised mandate to assert within a jurisdiction or domain, and the standing that mandate gives the claim, recorded without treating standing as truth.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Mandates are instruments issued and maintained by the granting bodies; this model holds a reference and a standing classification only. Producing a local artifact would imply this register certifies authority, which it does not, and would create a competing copy of an external legal or institutional instrument.

layers.name: Record Provenance, Ownership and Rights
layers.description: How the claim record itself was produced and derived, who owns and stewards it, and under what rights it may be reused.

findings.name: Record Derivation and Attribution
findings.description: The lineage of the claim record: which source it was derived or quoted from, which primary source stands behind it, which agent or process extracted it, and which revision it succeeds.

findings.name: Ownership, Stewardship and Rights
findings.description: Which package owns the claim record, who stewards it, which roles may change it, and under what licence or rights the statement and the record may be reused.

bundles.name: Claim Relations and External Bindings
bundles.description: How claims stand to one another and how a claim binds to evidence, assessments and argument structures owned elsewhere.
bundles.rationale: AIF supplies the typology of inference, conflict and preference relations at the argument level and locates propositions as I-nodes; PROV supplies revision and invalidation; FAIR I3 requires qualified rather than bare references; schema.org documents that it defines no claim-to-claim relations, which makes this a real modelling need. Bindings must carry parameters only, since evidence, review and argument content are owned by other models.

layers.name: Typed Claim-to-Claim Relations
layers.description: Recorded relations between claim records: entailment and specialization, conflict, and preference or supersession, registered without being adjudicated.

findings.name: Entailment and Specialization
findings.description: Relations where one claim's content stands to another as implication, generalization, specialization or presupposition, recorded as qualified edges with the ground on which the relation is asserted.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are typed edges between records in the same register, matching the model's declared TYPED-EDGES link type. Externalising them would duplicate graph state and would tempt consumers to read a curated edge list as a derived inference result, which this model does not produce.

findings.name: Conflict and Contradiction
findings.description: Registration that two claims stand in conflict, with the conflict type and the point of disagreement recorded, and with resolution explicitly not performed here.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Conflicts are registered as qualified edges plus a registration event. A conflict register artifact would read as an adjudication docket and would encroach on the argumentation model that owns conflict-rule application and on the assessment systems that issue verdicts.

findings.name: Preference and Supersession
findings.description: Recorded orderings between claims: an asserted preference between competing claims, and the supersession chain by which a later claim replaces an earlier one.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Preference and supersession are directional edges evaluated at query time to find the current claim. Materialising a chain artifact would freeze a view that must stay derivable from the edges, and preference application in argument evaluation is owned by the argumentation model.

layers.name: External Bindings
layers.description: Qualified references from a claim to evidence items, external assessments and argument structures, carrying binding parameters only.

findings.name: Evidence Link Binding
findings.description: The qualified reference from this claim to an evidence item in WM-KNW-008, carrying the target identifier, the binding role, directionality and a locally stated binding weight, and nothing describing the evidence itself.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The binding is a qualified edge with a small parameter set, and by the REFERENCE contract with WM-KNW-008 nothing describing the evidence may be held locally. Any artifact here would inevitably accrete evidence metadata and would duplicate the target model's records.

findings.name: Assessment and Review Reference
findings.description: References from this claim to externally issued assessments, fact-checks or reviews of it, recorded so that consumers can find them without this model owning ratings, reviewer workflow or review audit trails.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Reviews are documents produced and governed by fact-checking and assessment systems. This model stores only resolvable references, because producing a local artifact would amount to republishing verdicts and would assert ownership of rating semantics and reviewer audit trails that belong to those systems.

findings.name: Argument Structure Role Reference
findings.description: The record that this claim occupies a premise or conclusion role in an externally identified argument structure, mapped to the AIF I-node level, without any local representation of inference-scheme application.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Only a role reference is held, because AIF rule-application nodes and scheme definitions belong to an argumentation model that is not yet registered. Producing an argument artifact here would create exactly the ownership overlap the boundary review is meant to prevent.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Validation and Record Governance
bundles.description: The states a claim record passes through, how it is versioned and corrected, how its well-formedness and quality are checked, and how it is restricted, retained and disposed of.
bundles.rationale: PROV supplies revision and invalidation semantics, NISO CREC supplies the metadata practice for externally issued retractions and expressions of concern, SHACL supplies shapes and severity-graded conformance separated from the processor, and ODRL supplies policy expression that explicitly excludes enforcement. These fix a governance surface for the record without claiming execution.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle and Change Control
layers.description: States and transitions of the claim record, the rule separating a new version from a new claim, and references to externally issued status notices.

findings.name: Status and State Transitions
findings.description: The permitted states of a claim record, the transitions between them, who may perform each transition, and the terminal timestamps and successor references that transitions set.

findings.name: Versioning and Change Control
findings.description: The rule distinguishing a version patch from a new claim, the immutability of asserted statement text, and the version manifest that lets any prior state of the record be reconstructed.

findings.name: Retraction, Correction and Status Notices
findings.description: References to notices issued outside this model — retractions, removals, corrections and expressions of concern — and the local status effect they trigger, with issuance and propagation remaining with the issuing publisher or authority.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Retraction and correction notices are artifacts created, published and propagated by publishers, aggregators and issuing authorities under their own recommended practice. This model records a reference and the local status effect only; producing a notice artifact here would claim issuance authority and would duplicate a document whose canonical version lives with its issuer.

layers.name: Validation and Quality
layers.description: Structural well-formedness of the claim record and the quality signals that indicate whether it is specific and testable enough to be useful.

findings.name: Well-Formedness, Quality and Testability
findings.description: The shapes and required-field profiles the record must satisfy, the severity grading of failures, and the quality signals — specificity, ambiguity, unresolved scope, testability — that gate promotion. Shapes are owned here; execution is not.

layers.name: Access, Sensitivity and Retention
layers.description: Classification of claim records by sensitivity, expression of access and use conditions, and the retention, tombstoning and disposition rules for the records this model owns.

findings.name: Sensitivity and Access Classification
findings.description: Classification of a claim record by the harm its statement could cause — unverified allegations, personal data, embargoed findings — and the expression of the resulting access and use conditions as a policy, with enforcement performed elsewhere.

findings.name: Retention and Disposition
findings.description: How long claim records are kept, what a tombstone must carry when a record is terminated or redacted, and which party owns execution of erasure across stores and downstream copies.

bundles.name: Interoperability and Agent Operation
bundles.description: How claim records project onto external vocabularies without claiming conformance, and how an agent bootstraps into the model and exchanges records safely.
bundles.rationale: Multiple standards model overlapping but non-identical notions of a claim: schema.org as a creative work, VC 2.0 as a subject-property-value assertion inside a credential, AIF as an I-node, nanopublications as an assertion graph, and RDF 1.2 as a triple term that may be named without being asserted. Recording these as alignments with declared losses, and providing an explicit bootstrap contract, is what makes the model operable by an agent.

layers.name: Alignment, Projection and Bootstrap
layers.description: Vocabulary crosswalks with lossiness declarations and statement-level projection choices, plus the agent bootstrap contract and exchange profile.

findings.name: Vocabulary Alignments and Projections
findings.description: Declared mappings from claim record fields to external vocabularies, the statement-level identity choice in each projection, and the explicit record of what each projection loses and where the standards conflict.

findings.name: Agent Bootstrap and Exchange Profile
findings.description: The bootstrap contract an agent reads before operating on claim records, the order in which it must read it, and the minimum interchange profile that any exchange of claim records must satisfy.

model.name: Evidence / Citation
model.purpose: Model the reified evidential citation: a directed, typed, attributable link from a citing context to a cited source, plus the locator needed to retrieve and re-verify the exact cited material.
model.scope_statement: Defines the evidential citation as an independently identifiable relationship record. Covers citing-context binding, evidential stance (support, challenge, qualification, neutral mention), evidence type and assertion method, the source locator (preferred citation identifier, access URI, in-resource anchor, consulted representation state), integrity and provenance of the citation act, binding of an external certainty scheme, record lifecycle and supersession, and interoperability profiles. Storage- and interface-neutral: JSON, RDF, Markdown, Git, MCP and document stores are projections. It masters neither endpoint: the citing claim or decision, and the cited work, are governed elsewhere.
in_scope: Reified citation record identity, deduplication and the directed citing-context to cited-source link
Typed evidential stance and rhetorical intent, with polarity and direction
Evidence type and assertion method, including human curation versus automated or model-derived extraction
Source locator: preferred citation identifier distinguished from access URI, with scheme normalization
In-resource anchoring by selector chains, plus excerpt, quotation context and transformation status
Consulted representation state: access datetime, version identifier, archived snapshot and request conditions
Locator resolution health, link rot and content drift detection
Binding of an externally governed certainty rating scheme and its per-domain limitation results
Provenance of the citation act, with event, observation and ingestion times kept separate
Fixity of excerpts and captures, and references to signed media provenance manifests
Citation record lifecycle states, supersession and versioning
Dated observations of the cited source's status such as retraction or expression of concern
Alignment declarations, exchange profiles and sensitivity classification of the record and its excerpt
out_of_scope: Claim wording, decomposition, truth status and lifecycle, which belong to WM-KNW-007
Decision options, criteria, deliberation and decision lifecycle, which belong to WM-KNW-010
Aggregation of multiple evidence items into a verdict, belief revision, or argument-scheme structure
Canonical bibliographic description and the publication lifecycle of the cited work
Web archive capture scheduling, storage and preservation execution
Rendering of style-specific formatted reference strings and bibliographies
Runtime access evaluation, enforcement and audit-trail records
Execution of retention schedules, erasure and legal-hold determination
Publisher or author trust and reputation scoring as a managed registry
Signing and cryptographic validation of media provenance manifests
Bibliometric citation counting and impact analytics

boundary_notes.distinction: The claim model owns claim identity, text, decomposition, status and lifecycle. This model holds only a resolving reference to the claim and a locus within it, and never mirrors or versions claim status.

The decision model owns options, criteria, rationale structure and decision lifecycle. This model supplies citation records that a rationale step points at; it models no deliberation and reaches no conclusion.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Bibliographic source-work registry (DataCite, Crossref or equivalent)
boundary_notes.distinction: Registries master full bibliographic metadata and identifier authority. This model holds a cached, explicitly non-authoritative minimal descriptor with a refresh timestamp, sufficient to make a citation intelligible without dereferencing.
This model records memento and timegate URIs, archive datetimes and digests. Capture scheduling, storage tiers and preservation actions are external.
Provenance patterns are used for the citation act only. A whole-of-knowledge-base activity and agent graph is a separate concern and is not constructed here.
This model records one typed evidential link with stance and certainty. Multi-premise schemes, defeaters, weighting and aggregation are not modelled.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Adopting-Dimension access policy and audit service
boundary_notes.distinction: Only sensitivity labels and policy references are held here. Evaluation of a request, enforcement and the audit trail are owned entirely by that service; referencing an audit event grants no ownership of audit semantics.
Signed manifests and hard or soft bindings are referenced as integrity evidence for media excerpts. Signing, certificate handling and validation are performed by that system.
This model records a retention class reference, disposition state and tombstone stub. Schedule ownership, legal-hold determination and erasure execution stay with the adopting Dimension.

functions.name: Mint citation record
functions.description: Create a reified citation record linking a citing context to a cited source with a typed stance.
inputs: Cited source identifier or access URI
Stance code and bound vocabulary version
preconditions: The citing-context reference resolves in its owning model
The stance vocabulary version is bound
The asserting agent is identified and its kind declared
Deduplication key computed and checked
effects: Creates a citation record in the proposed state
Links to an existing record instead of minting a duplicate when the deduplication key matches
Leaves the citing context and the cited source unmodified

functions.name: Resolve source locator
functions.description: Resolve a preferred citation identifier or access URI to a retrievable representation, optionally at a target datetime.
inputs: Preferred citation identifier or access URI
Optional target datetime for time-based access
outputs: Discovered preferred citation identifier where advertised
preconditions: At least one identifier or URI is present
Resolver and time gate endpoints are reachable or their failure is recordable
effects: Records the resolution outcome and any redirect chain
Populates the preferred citation identifier when a preferred-reference link is advertised by the source
Sets locator health state

functions.name: Anchor cited excerpt
functions.description: Attach selectors and an excerpt locating the cited portion within a retrieved representation.
outputs: Excerpt with prefix and suffix context
preconditions: A representation has been retrieved
A canonicalization profile is declared
Licence and privacy limits on excerpting have been checked
effects: Attaches selectors and the excerpt to the record
Flags whole-resource granularity with a reason when finer anchoring is impossible
Suppresses excerpt text where reproduction is not permitted while retaining selectors and digest

functions.name: Capture representation state
functions.description: Record the state of the representation consulted, including access datetime, version, archived snapshot and fixity.
inputs: Archive or time gate endpoint where available
outputs: Access timestamp and any archive datetime
preconditions: The retention class permits storing a capture
The licence permits retaining a copy of the representation
effects: Stores a point-in-time capture with its digest and media type
Records the archived snapshot and time gate references
Does not schedule or perform ongoing archiving, which remains with the archiving service

functions.name: Classify evidential link
functions.description: Assign stance, evidence type and assertion method to the citation record.
inputs: Stance vocabulary and evidence-type vocabulary with versions
outputs: Assertion method code and machine confidence where automated
preconditions: An anchor exists at some granularity
Both vocabularies and their versions are declared by the owning package
effects: Sets the typed classification on the record
Records tool and model version when the classification was produced automatically
Blocks promotion beyond draft when the minimum granularity rule is unmet

functions.name: Assess evidential certainty
functions.description: Bind an external certainty scheme and record a certainty value with its per-domain limitation results.
preconditions: The scheme is externally defined and version-bound
The assessor is identified and independence is declared
effects: Attaches a new assessment or supersedes a prior one for the same scheme
Never redefines or extends the external scheme's own definitions
Marks the assessment provisional when domain judgements are incomplete

functions.name: Re-verify citation and detect drift
functions.description: Re-resolve the locator, re-apply selectors, recompute digests and confirm the asserted stance still holds.
outputs: Recomputed digests and anchor match result
preconditions: A locator is present
Prior digests or an excerpt exist for comparison
The verifier is identified
effects: Appends a verification report and sets verification validity
Sets locator health and may raise a content-drifted or contested flag
Never modifies the citing context, whose own status remains with its owning model

functions.name: Record cited-source status observation
functions.description: Record a dated observation that the cited source has been retracted, corrected, removed, flagged or superseded.
outputs: Event time at the source and observation time here
preconditions: A status authority or feed for the source is identified
The event time and observation time can be distinguished or the gap explained
effects: Appends a dated observation to the record
May raise a review flag and notify the citing model through its own interface
Does not assert, execute or publish the source's retraction, which belongs to the source's publisher

functions.name: Supersede or withdraw citation record
functions.description: Create a successor version or withdraw a record, preserving resolvability of the predecessor.
outputs: New record version or withdrawn state
preconditions: The acting agent holds a declared permitted action for supersession or withdrawal
No legal hold forbids the change
Immutable fields are respected
effects: Creates a successor version and marks the predecessor superseded while keeping it resolvable
Records reason, actor and timestamp on both versions
Leaves the citing context to decide what its own status becomes

functions.name: Project record to an exchange profile
functions.description: Produce a profile-conformant projection of a citation record for exchange with another system.
preconditions: A crosswalk exists for the target vocabulary version
Profile obligations are declared
Disclosure scope permits export of each included component
effects: Emits the projection with suppressed components marked rather than silently dropped
Records unmapped local terms and round-trip loss
Asserts conformance only where a valid conformance test result exists

functions.name: Mark record disposition
functions.description: Apply a disposition state, redaction markers and tombstone stub on instruction from the owning retention service.
inputs: Retention class decision from the adopting Dimension
Legal hold status from the owning service
preconditions: The retention class reference resolves
Legal hold status has been checked with its owning service
The surviving stub element set is declared
effects: Sets disposition state and reduces the record to a resolvable stub
Redacts or purges excerpts and captures while retaining selectors, digests and identifiers
Leaves schedule ownership, erasure execution and hold determination with the adopting Dimension's records service

composition.purpose: Carry a resolving reference to the claim that is supported or challenged, plus the locus within it. Claim wording, decomposition, truth status and lifecycle stay in the claim model and are never mirrored here.
Let a rationale step point at citation records for explainability. Options, criteria, deliberation and decision lifecycle remain owned by the decision model.
Resolve asserting agents, verifiers, accountable organisations and responsible parties instead of mastering person or organisation records in this model.

composition.target: Bibliographic source-work registry (DataCite, Crossref or equivalent)
composition.purpose: Dereference full bibliographic metadata and identifier authority for the cited work. Only a non-authoritative minimal descriptor with a refresh timestamp is cached locally.

composition.target: Web archiving service conforming to the Memento framework
composition.purpose: Record archived snapshot and time gate URIs with archive datetimes. Capture scheduling, storage and preservation actions remain with the archiving service.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension access policy and audit service
composition.purpose: Hold sensitivity labels and policy references only. Request evaluation, enforcement and audit-trail records are owned entirely by that service; referencing an audit event confers no ownership of audit semantics.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension records retention and disposition service
composition.purpose: Bind a retention class, receive disposition instructions and read legal-hold status. Schedule ownership, hold determination and erasure execution stay outside this model.
Map local stance values onto CiTO citation properties and adopt its reified citation pattern. Alignment only, with conflicts and unmapped terms recorded.
Express the citation act as entity, activity and agent for provenance interchange, without importing a general provenance graph for the wider knowledge base.
Adopt the selector, refinement and state patterns for in-resource anchoring and consulted-representation binding, normalising timestamps at the boundary.
Map citation direction, versioning and obsolescence relations onto a governed relation vocabulary for scholarly exchange, recording the loss where challenge stances have no equivalent.
Bind evidence-type and assertion-method values, declaring local extension terms explicitly where the target's biomedical scope does not reach.
Bind an externally governed certainty scale and its rate-down and rate-up domains as an assessment scheme, without redefining or extending the scheme itself.
Reference signed media provenance manifests and their hard or soft bindings as integrity evidence for media excerpts. Signing, certificate handling and validation are performed by that system.
Align cited-source status observations with the recommended retraction, removal and expression-of-concern metadata and its propagation to citing works.
Map web-publication fact-check linkage, making explicit that the verdict rating sits with the citing claim model while only stance is carried here.

owner_package_requirements: The owning package must declare the stance, evidence-type and certainty vocabularies it binds, each with a resolvable reference and an explicit version.
The owning package must name the master system for citation record identifiers and the fallback identifier scheme it mints when no master system exists.
The owning package must name the retention and disposition service, the access policy and audit service, and the party model it delegates to, since this model owns none of them.
The owning package must declare which citing-context models are permitted endpoints and how their references resolve.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local record identifiers and local controlled values are minted in a Dimension-scoped namespace and never inside an external standard's namespace. External terms are referenced by their governing IRI together with the version in force. Local extensions to an aligned vocabulary live under a clearly separated local extension path so that a consumer can distinguish standard terms from local ones without a lookup.
registry_links: DataCite Metadata Schema relationType as the governed vocabulary for citation direction, versioning and obsolescence relations.
SPAR CiTO property set as the governed citation-intent vocabulary for supporting and challenging stances.
The cite-as link relation as the governed mechanism for discovering a source's preferred citation identifier.
Evidence and Conclusion Ontology as the governed evidence-type and assertion-method vocabulary where scientific evidence is cited.
The GRADE certainty framework as a bindable external certainty scheme.

canonicalization_rules: Declare a canonicalization profile before digesting any excerpt: a fixed Unicode normalization form, defined whitespace folding, a defined line-ending form, and explicit inclusion or exclusion of prefix and suffix context in the digest input.

Normalize identifiers before comparison or deduplication: consistent case for scheme and prefix, resolver host removed, percent-encoding normalized; retain both the raw and normalized forms so the original is never lost.
Serialize all timestamps in the canonical form and sort repeated elements by a declared stable key before digesting, so that logically equal records produce equal digests across projections.
patch_rules: Patches address individual elements by stable path and never reorder or renumber collections as a side effect of an unrelated change.
Any patch that alters stance, locator, anchor, excerpt, fixity or certainty on an asserted record produces a new record version rather than an in-place edit.
Every patch carries a change reason code, the acting agent reference and an ingestion timestamp; a patch without a reason code is rejected.
A patch may not write a value into an element owned by a referenced model, such as claim status or audit outcome; such a patch is rejected at the boundary.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element or a new controlled value is a minor change. Removing an element, narrowing cardinality or retiring a controlled value is breaking and requires a new profile major version.
Retired controlled values remain resolvable and carry a mapping to their replacement rather than being deleted.
A conformance claim against an external vocabulary version is invalidated when that version changes and must be re-tested before it is restated.

identity_priority: The authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the citation, such as the curation platform's citation record key, is used first and is never re-minted locally.
Where no master-system identifier exists, a governed global identifier or IRI such as a DOI, Handle or registered persistent IRI, resolvable through its own registry, is used.
Only when neither exists does the adopting Dimension assign a UUID or ULID in its own namespace. A date, a URL that may change, and a content digest are never used as the primary identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded in RFC 3339 form with an explicit seconds component and an explicit offset or Z, for example 2026-09-02T14:03:07Z or 2026-09-02T16:03:07+02:00, using -00:00 only to signal a known UTC instant whose local offset is unknown. Event time (when the assertion was made, when the cited source was published, changed or retracted) is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time (when the representation was accessed, when the status was observed, when the record entered this store); where only one is known the other is left empty rather than copied across. Protocol formats that use another representation, such as the RFC 1123 datetimes carried in time-based access headers, are converted to this form on storage.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely excerpt captures, consulted-representation captures, locator check reports and verification reports, are named as the citation record identifier plus a zero-padded ordinal that increases monotonically and is never reused, even after a member is deleted. Capture datetimes, verifier names and digests are attributes of the artifact and never form part of its name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored artifact carries a named digest algorithm, a digest value computed after the declared canonicalization profile, a byte size and a media type. A recomputation mismatch sets the artifact to an integrity-failed state and marks dependent verification results stale; the artifact and its original digest are retained as evidence of the mismatch rather than silently replaced.

policies: Conformance to an external standard is asserted only where a dated test result or authoritative registration is recorded. Otherwise the relationship is recorded as an alignment with its known conflicts and round-trip losses.
A citation record never restates, caches as authoritative, or version-controls the content or status of the citing claim or decision it points at; those remain mastered by their owning models.
Automatically generated citations are marked with their assertion method, tool and model version, and may not enter a verified state without a recorded independent verification pass.

Excerpts are stored only within licence and privacy limits. Where reproduction is not permitted, the locator, selectors and digests are retained without the excerpt text, so the citation stays re-verifiable at the source.
This model records references to policy, hold and audit artefacts but never evaluates, enforces or writes them.

read: Reading a record returns identity, locator, stance, provenance and current state. Excerpts and captures are returned only where the requester's disclosure scope permits, with suppressed components explicitly marked.
Superseded, withdrawn and tombstoned records remain readable by identifier, returning state, reason and successor link so that historical citing contexts never dangle.
A read may specify a target datetime to obtain the record version that was current at that instant, distinguishing what was asserted then from what is asserted now.
create: A record may be created only with a resolving citing-context reference, at least one source identifier or access URI, a stance value drawn from a version-bound vocabulary, and an identified asserting agent.
Creation sets ingestion time from the receiving system clock and assertion time from the assertion event; the two are stored separately and never conflated.
Duplicate detection runs on the normalized deduplication key before minting; a match returns a link to the existing record rather than creating a second one.
update: Non-evidential fields such as notes, review cadence and the cached source descriptor may be updated in place with a change reason and acting agent.
Changes to stance, locator, anchor, excerpt, fixity or certainty on an asserted record produce a new version with supersession links; the prior version becomes immutable.
State transitions follow only the declared permitted transitions and always record reason, actor and timestamp.
Elements owned by referenced models, including claim status, decision outcome, hold determination and audit entries, are never written by this model.
delete: Hard deletion is not performed by this model. A record leaving service is set to withdrawn or disposed and reduced to a tombstone stub retaining the record identifier, final state, disposition reason, disposition timestamp and successor link, so that citing contexts resolve rather than break.

Excerpts, representation captures and any personal data inside them may be redacted or purged ahead of the record itself. Selectors, digests and identifiers survive redaction so the citation remains re-verifiable against the original source, and each redaction is marked with its basis.

The retention class, the disposition schedule, the legal-hold determination and the authority to order erasure are owned by the adopting Dimension's records retention and disposition service. This model records only the class reference, the hold reference, the disposition state and the resulting stub, and executes disposition markers on that service's instruction.

Where a takedown obliges removal of cited content, this model removes only its own copies and observations. Removal at the source is executed by the source's publisher, repository or archiving service and is never performed or claimed here.

roles.name: Citation asserter
responsibilities: Create citation records with a resolving citing-context reference, a stance value and a locator
Declare the assertion method and, for automated assertion, the tool and model version
Capture the excerpt within licence and privacy limits, or record why it was suppressed

roles.name: Evidence verifier
responsibilities: Re-resolve locators, re-apply selectors and compare digests
Confirm or reject the asserted stance and record a dated verification report
Raise contested and drift flags without altering the citing context

roles.name: Vocabulary and alignment steward
responsibilities: Maintain the bound stance, evidence-type and certainty vocabularies and their versions
Own the crosswalks to external vocabularies and record conflicts and round-trip losses
Re-test conformance claims whenever a target vocabulary version changes

roles.name: Record owner
responsibilities: Accept accountability for the record, its review cadence and its disposition state
Approve supersession and withdrawal
Resolve disputes over stance through the declared escalation path

roles.name: Locator custodian
responsibilities: Schedule and interpret resolution health checks
Register fallback locators and archived snapshot references
Escalate link rot and content drift to the record owner

access.default_rule: A citation record defaults to the more restrictive of the citing context's sensitivity and the cited source's disclosure terms. Identity, locator and stance metadata are readable at the citing context's scope, while excerpts and stored captures default to origin-only disclosure until a broader scope is explicitly granted by the adopting Dimension's policy service.
exceptions: Embargoed source: locator and stance remain readable while the excerpt and captures stay withheld until the embargo timestamp lapses.
Personal or special-category data in an excerpt: the excerpt is masked or withheld while selectors and digests remain readable so re-verification is still possible.
Licence-restricted reproduction: excerpt text is suppressed on export outside the origin while the citation record itself is exported with a suppression marker.
Legal hold: disposition actions are blocked even after the retention class has expired, on instruction from the owning retention service.
Contested or integrity-failed records: readable with their flag visible; the flag may not be stripped on export.
audit_requirements: Every state transition, supersession, verification and disposition action records the acting agent, reason code and an RFC 3339 timestamp on the record itself.

Disclosure of an excerpt or capture outside its default scope is recorded as an event by the adopting Dimension's audit service; this model stores only a reference to that event and never the audit trail.
Automated assertion and automated verification passes are attributable to a named tool and version so that a later reviewer can reproduce them.
Alignment and conformance claims record who authored them, against which target version they were tested, and when they were last reviewed.

required_fields: Delegation targets for party, retention, access and audit
read_order: AGENTS.md for the model name, type and the four mandatory URLs
Specification URL for scope, boundaries, exclusions and the bundle, layer and finding structure
Storage type URL for the projection in force and its canonicalization profile
Interface URL for read, create, update and disposition operations and their preconditions
Processes URL for the assertion, verification, supersession and disposition procedures
Composition links to the citing-context, party, retention, access and audit services before any write is attempted

coverage.claim: Within its 13 cited sources the draft covers the reified evidential citation: record identity and deduplication, stance and evidence typing, preferred-citation-identifier versus access-URI separation, in-resource anchoring and excerpt handling, consulted-representation state and drift detection, citation-act provenance and fixity, binding of an external certainty scheme, lifecycle and supersession, and declaration-level access, retention and exchange. Coverage is single-provider and uncorroborated. Aggregation, adjudication, bibliographic mastering and runtime enforcement are excluded by design; legal admissibility and sub-sentence multilingual alignment remain declared gaps. No claim of completeness for evidence semantics generally.

checklist.notes: Reified citation record with its own identifier, master-system-first identity priority, deduplication key and equivalence to external citation identifiers. Grounded in the reified citation pattern in CiTO and the identified annotation in the Web Annotation model.

State enumeration, permitted transitions, immutability on assertion, versioning and supersession, and disposition states. Validity intervals follow the Verifiable Credentials pattern; the citing context's own lifecycle is explicitly excluded.
Citing-context binding with locus, directed stance link with optional inverse, supersession links, opposing-record references and alignment to a governed relation vocabulary.

Assertion, ingestion, access, archive, status-event, status-observation, assessment, verification and embargo times are modelled separately under a single RFC 3339 profile with an explicit seconds component and offset.
Asserting agent, accountable organisation, delegation chain and activity follow the PROV entity-activity-agent pattern; tool and model version are required for automated assertion.
Record owner, steward, accountable organisation and the mastering registry for bibliographic metadata are all named, with an explicit non-authority flag on the cached descriptor.

Selector re-anchoring, digest recomputation, timestamp ordering checks, stance confirmation and profile conformance tests, with an explicit rule that unevidenced conformance is recorded only as alignment.

Sensitivity classes, component-level disclosure scopes, embargo and licence references are modelled as declarations. Evaluation, enforcement and the access log are referenced and explicitly disclaimed.

No hard delete: withdrawal and disposition produce a resolvable tombstone stub; excerpts and captures may be redacted ahead of the record. Schedule ownership, hold determination and erasure execution belong to the adopting Dimension's records service.
Term-level crosswalks with mapping strength and recorded loss, an exchange profile with obligations and extension rules, and explicit conversion of protocol-format timestamps at the boundary.
Preferred citation identifier separated from access URI, archived snapshot and time gate references, fallback locators, scheduled resolution checks and content drift detection.
An external certainty scheme is bound by version with per-domain limitation results; the scheme itself is never redefined, and no local scale is invented.
Canonicalization before digesting, digests over excerpt and representation, integrity-failed state, and references to signed media provenance manifests for media excerpts.
Weighing multiple evidence items into a verdict belongs to the claim and decision models. Only opposing-record references and a contested flag are held here, by design.
Citation counting, co-citation and impact analytics are downstream computations over these records rather than evidential context, and are excluded to keep the record semantically neutral.

checklist.dimension: legal admissibility and chain of custody
checklist.notes: Jurisdiction-specific custody, sealing, disclosure and admissibility duties are not modelled. No cited authority in this source set governs them, so the structure would be unsupported.
Language tagging and a translation flag are present, but transliteration schemes, script variants and sub-sentence alignment between an original and its translation are not modelled.

known_omissions: No model of citation counting or bibliometric aggregation; these are downstream analytics over citation records, not evidential context.
No jurisdiction-specific chain-of-custody or admissibility model for legal or forensic evidence, which would impose custody, sealing and disclosure duties this model does not express.
Multilingual coverage stops at language tagging and a transformation flag; transliteration, script variants and original-to-translation alignment below sentence level are absent.

Citations to inherently non-retrievable sources such as personal communications, oral testimony and embargoed internal documents are supported only at whole-resource granularity with a descriptor and no persistent identifier.
Rights and licensing of the cited source are referenced but not modelled; machine-enforceable reuse terms would require a separate rights model.
Confidence values reported by automated extractors are stored as opaque numbers with a declared scale but no governed calibration methodology.
No model of evidence sampling or corpus construction, so systematic selection bias across a set of citations cannot be detected from these records alone.
conflicts: CiTO version is reported as 2.8.2 in the current SPAR documentation build while other SPAR pages and secondary indexes cite 2.8.1 dated 16 February 2018. Any binding must pin the version explicitly and re-check it before a conformance claim is restated.

The Memento framework mandates RFC 1123 datetimes in its Accept-Datetime and Memento-Datetime headers, whereas this model requires RFC 3339 for stored values. Implementations must convert at the protocol boundary and store the RFC 3339 form, keeping the original header value only as provenance.

The Web Annotation Data Model requires created and modified timestamps expressed in UTC with a trailing Z, while RFC 3339 permits non-zero offsets. Export to Web Annotation normalises to UTC and loses the original local offset unless it is retained in a separate element.

CiTO citation intents and DataCite relationTypes overlap only partially: DataCite offers Cites, IsCitedBy and Reviews but no equivalent of refutes, disputes or qualifies, so challenge stances cannot round-trip through DataCite without loss.

schema.org ClaimReview places the verdict rating on the review, while this model keeps the verdict with the citing claim model and carries only stance. A mapping must decide explicitly which side holds the rating, and the decision must be recorded in the crosswalk.

ECO was developed for biological assertions and its assertion-method branch does not fully cover legal, journalistic or engineering evidence; local extension terms are required and must be declared as local rather than presented as ECO terms.

GRADE certainty levels are defined for effect estimates in health evidence. Applying them to documentary, testimonial or engineering evidence is an extension beyond the handbook's stated scope and must be declared as such rather than claimed as GRADE conformance.
regional_assumptions: Assumes no single jurisdiction's law of evidence applies. Where the adopting Dimension operates under a specific regime, such as a national records act or a regional data protection law, its retention, redaction and disclosure obligations override the defaults stated here.

Assumes scholarly identifier infrastructure such as DOI, Handle and PMID is reachable. Where it is not, the governed-global-identifier tier of the identity priority collapses to Dimension-assigned identifiers and the locator becomes correspondingly weaker.

Assumes that retaining an archived copy of the cited representation is lawful and permitted by licence. Some publishers and some jurisdictions restrict archival copies, which forces locator-only citations without a capture.
Assumes excerpts are stored in the source's original language by default. Localised deployments must declare their own default language and translation policy.

Assumes the adopting Dimension operates a party model, a retention service and an access policy service; where any is absent, the corresponding references become unresolvable and the model degrades to declarations without delegation targets.
adversarial_checks: Boundary test against WM-KNW-007: no bundle, layer, finding or function stores claim text, claim decomposition, claim truth status or claim lifecycle. The model carries only a citing-context reference and locus, and the contested flag deliberately stops short of adjudication, which is stated as an explicit deferred judgement.

Boundary test against WM-KNW-010: nothing here models options, criteria, deliberation or decision outcome. The decision model consumes citation records and retains its own rationale lifecycle; no function writes back into it.

Runtime-ownership test: sensitivity classes, retention classes, legal holds and audit events appear only as references. No finding or function defines an evaluation engine, an enforcement point or an audit trail, and the delete rules name the adopting Dimension as the executor of erasure and hold determination.

Counterexample test on non-retrievable sources: personal communications and oral testimony have no resolvable identifier, so identifier elements are optional, an explicit no-identifier exception question exists, and whole-resource anchor granularity is a first-class recorded outcome rather than a failure.

Counterexample test on sources that change after citation: drift is detectable only if a digest and a capture existed at assertion time, so fixity and consulted-representation capture are modelled as first-class rather than optional convenience, and integrity failure is a retained state rather than a silent overwrite.

Duplication test against bibliographic registries: source metadata appears only as an explicitly non-authoritative cache with a refresh timestamp and a named master, preventing this model from becoming a shadow bibliographic registry.

Unsupported-structure test: a publisher or author trust-score layer was considered and rejected because no source in this set defines a governed trust vocabulary; certainty is bound to an external, version-pinned scheme instead, and no local scale was invented.

Format-neutrality test: no finding names a serialization. Selectors, states, digests and profiles are described as semantics, with JSON, RDF, Markdown, Git, MCP and document stores treated as projections governed by the canonicalization rules.

providerPolicy.scope: Queued subject-model research from WM-XCT-013 onward

waived_providers.reason: The repository owner explicitly instructed the research queue to continue without Grok after repeated structured-output failures.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Claude-only results require a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remain reviewable drafts with a visible single-provider hold.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must be kept apart. The frozen registry value standalone-mm classifies the record plane (a world-model record carried standalone in the registry, per record_plane world-model) and is not a member of the subject-model enum, so it cannot be adopted here. On the subject-model axis the defining semantic is a directed, typed, attributable link from a citing context to a cited source that masters neither endpoint: both contract edges (WM-KNW-007 and WM-KNW-010) are inbound REFERENCE, contains_ids and composition_role are empty, and every boundary note reasserts non-ownership of both ends. 'relationship' is therefore the most defensible schema kind. 'aggregate' was considered because the record has independent identity, lifecycle, supersession and four identity-dependent serial artifacts keyed on the record identifier; that behaviour is a consequence of reification, not a change of kind, and 'entity' was rejected because the record has no meaning detached from its two endpoints.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root identification: citation record as root of captures, check reports and verification reports
decisions.rationale: All four serial artifacts key on the citation record identifier plus a never-reused zero-padded ordinal, matching serial_naming_rule exactly; no member carries independent identity, so the root is unambiguous and no member can be orphaned or re-parented.

decisions.concept: Deduplication key composition versus the identity finding's distinguishability claim
decisions.rationale: The create rule collapses a mint onto an existing record when a normalized key matches, but the key's composition is left entirely to open question q-cri-definition. Unless the key includes locus, stance and asserting agent, it contradicts the identity finding's own claim that a record is distinguishable from any other link between the same two endpoints.

decisions.concept: Evidence assessment record identity (record id + scheme id + scheme version, serial:false)
decisions.rationale: q-cal-provenance requires recording assessor independence and q-saa-constraint requires a review cadence for high-consequence citations, so two independent assessments under one scheme version are expected; the declared key collides on them. A never-reused occurrence component is needed without promoting datetime or digest to the key.

decisions.concept: Vocabulary crosswalk identity keyed on the target vocabulary's own version string
decisions.rationale: SRC-009 records no ECO release version on the registry page and SRC-010 carries only 'Updated October 2013', so the declared key is unsatisfiable for two of the five registry_links vocabularies. A declared surrogate version token with its derivation rule is required before the identity strategy is published as normative.

decisions.concept: GRADE certainty binding applied at single-citation granularity
decisions.rationale: GRADE rates certainty for a body of evidence per outcome, while this model excludes aggregation entirely; the conflicts list acknowledges the domain extension but not the unit-of-assessment mismatch. The binding must record the scheme's own unit of assessment alongside the version pin.

decisions.concept: Fixity values and selectors surviving redaction of personal-data excerpts
decisions.disposition: accepted for draft, held for privacy review
decisions.rationale: The delete rule states unconditionally that selectors and digests survive redaction so re-verification stays possible. Over a short special-category excerpt a retained digest remains a checkable value, and regional_assumptions only defer generically to overriding regimes rather than qualifying this specific rule.

decisions.concept: Access scope enumeration (bundle, layer, finding, artifact) versus record, excerpt and capture disclosure rules
decisions.rationale: The enumerated scopes are documentation-structure levels while the default rule, exceptions and q-aac-access all govern instance components. Only 'artifact' maps cleanly to a capture; the mismatch must be annotated in the draft rather than published as a coherent scope vocabulary.

decisions.concept: Contested-flag procedure with a role responsibility and a question but no function
decisions.rationale: The Evidence verifier role must raise contested and drift flags and q-cce-process asks who runs the raise, review and clear procedure, yet none of the 11 functions covers it. Single-provider mode forbids adding a function, so this is recorded as an open structural gap rather than invented.

decisions.concept: Alignment authoring and conformance re-test with no covering function
decisions.rationale: The compatibility rule invalidates a conformance claim when a target version changes and the steward role must re-test it, but the function set only projects a record to an exchange profile. The maintenance path for the crosswalk artifact is therefore unexecutable as specified.

decisions.concept: Registry parent_ids WM-KNW-007 versus the REFERENCE-only relationship contract
decisions.rationale: contains_ids, composition_role and default_link_type are empty and both contract edges point inward as REFERENCE. A compositional reading of parent_ids would contradict the model's independent identity, lifecycle and supersession, so it must be read as taxonomy placement under NAV.INF.KNW.EVD.

decisions.concept: Checklist rows 'access' and 'retention and deletion' marked covered
decisions.rationale: The model explicitly disclaims request evaluation, enforcement, the audit trail, schedule ownership, hold determination and erasure execution. An unqualified 'covered' overstates what the record supplies and invites an adopter to assume delegation targets exist.

decisions.concept: Cited-source arity of a single citation record
decisions.rationale: q-ccb-constraint governs whether one record may serve several citing contexts, but nothing constrains the cited-source side. With aggregation and argument schemes out of scope, one cited source per record should be stated explicitly rather than left inferable.

decisions.concept: SRC-012 schema.org ClaimReview as the sole tier-3 mapping target
decisions.rationale: It carries a fast-moving version string (30.0, 19 March 2026) and drives the declared conflict over whether the verdict rating sits on the review or with the citing claim model; that crosswalk decision cannot be restated without re-verifying the pinned version.

decisions.concept: Rejection of a local publisher or author trust-score layer
decisions.rationale: The unsupported-structure adversarial check is sound: no source in the set defines a governed trust vocabulary, and binding certainty to an external version-pinned scheme instead of inventing a local scale is the correct discipline for a source-grounded model.

publicationHolds: Live source and version verification is outstanding for all 13 sources. SRC-003 (CiTO 2.8.2 versus the 2.8.1 dated 2018 cited elsewhere), SRC-009 (ECO, no release version recorded at all), SRC-010 (GRADE handbook, 'Updated October 2013' only), SRC-011 (C2PA 2.2), SRC-012 (schema.org 30.0) and SRC-008 (VC Data Model 2.0) must each be re-resolved and re-pinned before any alignment or conformance claim is restated in a published artifact.

Independent second-provider review is absent by explicit owner authorization: Grok was waived by the repository owner at 2026-08-29T09:06:27Z after repeated structured-output failures. Every publication artifact must carry a visible single-provider hold, name the waived provider and the authorizing party, and the result remains a reviewable draft rather than an adjudicated model.

Registry status candidate and review_state boundary-review-required must remain in force until the parent_ids link to WM-KNW-007 is confirmed as navigational placement rather than composition, since a compositional reading would invalidate the accepted relationship entry kind.

The normalized deduplication key composition must be bound (locus, stance and asserting agent at minimum) before any implementation or interface guidance is published, because the create rule as written can silently merge legitimately distinct assertions.

The evidence-assessment-record identity strategy must gain a never-reused occurrence component before the artifact identity rules are published as normative, otherwise an independent re-assessment under the same scheme version is unrepresentable.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Pin a resolvable ECO release IRI or dated version for SRC-009 and record the derivation rule for the surrogate version token used in the crosswalk artifact key.

Resolve the CiTO version discrepancy (2.8.2 in the current SPAR build versus 2.8.1 dated 16 February 2018 in secondary indexes) against the namespace itself and record which build the stance mapping was tested against.

Verify whether any later IETF specification updates or profiles RFC 3339 in a way that affects the declared timestamp rule, particularly the -00:00 convention and the RFC 1123 conversion at the Memento protocol boundary.
Define the normalized deduplication key and its interaction with q-cri-definition, then re-test it against the case of two opposing-stance records over the same citing context.

Determine how the unconditional survival of excerpt digests through redaction interacts with erasure obligations over short special-category excerpts, and whether a salted or truncated fixity form preserves re-verifiability without preserving a checkable value.

Assign ownership and a procedure for raising, reviewing and clearing the contested flag, and reconcile it with the Evidence verifier role responsibilities before any function is added in a future multi-provider pass.
Specify the alignment authoring and conformance re-test path required by the compatibility rule and the Vocabulary and alignment steward role, which currently has no covering function.

Identify an authoritative source for jurisdiction-neutral chain-of-custody and admissibility duties, or confirm the gap is unclosable from any defensible source set, before the legal-admissibility checklist row is revisited.
Establish whether the schema.org ClaimReview verdict rating sits with the review or with the citing claim model, and record the decision explicitly in the crosswalk as the conflicts list requires.

bundles.name: Evidential Link Identity and Typing
bundles.description: The citation as a reified, independently identifiable relationship, what it attaches to, and how its evidential character is typed.
bundles.rationale: CiTO reifies a citation as a directed link with its own characterization, and the Web Annotation model reifies an annotation with its own identity; both require the link to be addressable independently of its endpoints so that stance, provenance and lifecycle can attach to it.

layers.name: Citation Record Core
layers.description: Identity of the citation record and its binding to the citing context.

findings.name: Citation record identity and deduplication
findings.description: The evidential citation is a first-class record with its own identifier, distinguishable from any other link between the same two endpoints.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Record identity is pure structured reference data resolved through identifier registries. Materialising it as a separate file would create a second identity surface competing with the master system, which the identity priority explicitly forbids.

findings.name: Citing-context binding and locus
findings.description: What is doing the citing (claim, decision rationale, document passage or data field) and where inside it the citation applies, held as a reference only.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The binding is a pointer plus a locus expression. Producing an artifact here would duplicate content owned by WM-KNW-007 or WM-KNW-010 and create a second, drifting copy of the citing text.

layers.name: Evidential Typing
layers.description: Stance, intent, evidence type and the method by which the evidential assertion was produced.

findings.name: Evidential stance and citation intent
findings.description: The controlled value characterising whether the cited material supports, challenges, qualifies or merely mentions the citing context, with polarity and direction.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Stance is a single controlled value plus vocabulary binding. It is consumed by machines as a code, and rendering it as a document would obscure the version binding that makes it interpretable.

findings.name: Evidence type and assertion method
findings.description: What kind of evidence the cited material constitutes, and by what method the evidential link was produced: human curation, automated extraction or model inference.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are coded classifications and tool references. The pipeline configuration they point at is owned and versioned by the tooling package, so copying it here would fork a second configuration of record.

bundles.name: Cited Source Locator
bundles.description: Everything required to identify, retrieve, anchor and re-retrieve the exact cited material.
bundles.rationale: RFC 8574 separates the URI used for access from the URI preferred for citation, Memento provides time-based access to prior states, and the Web Annotation model supplies selector and state patterns; together these define what a durable source locator must carry.

layers.name: Source Identification
layers.description: Which source is cited, by which identifier, and what minimal description travels with it.

findings.name: Preferred citation identifier and scheme normalization
findings.description: The identifier that should be used to cite the source, kept distinct from the URI used to access it, with accepted schemes, precedence and normalization rules.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifiers and their normalized forms are atomic reference values that must stay comparable byte for byte. An artifact would add an indirection that defeats the deduplication and resolution rules built on them.

findings.name: Minimal source descriptor and its non-authority
findings.description: The smallest description held locally so a citation is intelligible without dereferencing, explicitly marked as a cache rather than the master record.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The descriptor exists only to make a reference legible in place; it is a bounded cache of registry-mastered fields. Emitting it as an artifact would encourage its reuse as a bibliographic record and turn this model into a shadow registry.

layers.name: In-Resource Anchoring
layers.description: Precise location of the cited portion inside the source, and the excerpt reproduced from it.

findings.name: Anchor selectors and granularity
findings.description: One or more selectors, optionally refined in a chain, that locate the cited portion within the retrieved representation, including non-textual regions.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Selectors are machine-evaluable expressions that must be applied against a representation at verification time. Freezing them into an artifact would separate them from the record whose re-anchoring they govern.

findings.name: Excerpt, quotation context and transformation
findings.description: The material actually reproduced from the source, with surrounding context, language, transformation status and reproduction limits.

layers.name: Consulted Representation State and Retrievability
layers.description: Which representation of the source was consulted, and whether the locator still resolves to equivalent content.

findings.name: Consulted representation state
findings.description: Binding of the citation to the specific representation consulted: access datetime, version, archived snapshot and the request conditions that produced it.

findings.name: Locator resolution health and content drift
findings.description: Whether the identifier still resolves, whether the anchored content is still present and unchanged, and how link rot and drift are recorded.

bundles.name: Evidential Assessment and Contest
bundles.description: How much confidence the cited material can carry, what limits it, and how contradiction and adverse source status are recorded without adjudicating.
bundles.rationale: GRADE defines an externally governed certainty scheme with explicit rate-down domains, and NISO CREC requires retraction status to propagate to citing works; both are properties the citation must carry, while the verdict remains with the citing model.

layers.name: Certainty and Limitations
layers.description: Binding of an external rating scheme and recording of assessed limitations.

findings.name: Certainty rating binding and limitation domains
findings.description: How much confidence the cited material provides for this citing context, expressed on an externally governed scheme with per-domain limitation results.

layers.name: Contest and Cited-Source Status
layers.description: Cross-references to opposing evidence, and dated observations about the cited source's editorial status.

findings.name: Contested flag and counter-evidence references
findings.description: Recording that other citation records address the same citing context with an opposing stance, without weighing them or reaching a conclusion.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding holds only cross-references and a flag. The evaluation that weighs opposing evidence and reaches a verdict belongs to the claim and decision models, so producing a local adjudication artifact would create a rival source of truth for a judgement this model does not own.

findings.name: Cited-source status observation
findings.description: Dated observations that the cited source has been retracted, withdrawn, corrected, flagged with an expression of concern or superseded, recorded as observations rather than as ownership of the source's lifecycle.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is a dated observation about a source whose lifecycle is governed by its publisher. The notice itself is published and persistently identified elsewhere, so this model stores the reference and the two timestamps rather than copying, re-issuing or re-asserting the notice.

bundles.name: Provenance and Integrity of the Citation Act
bundles.description: Who asserted the citation, when, with what tooling, and how the stored evidence is kept tamper-evident and independently verifiable.
bundles.rationale: PROV-O supplies the entity, activity and agent pattern for attributing an assertion; the Verifiable Credentials model separates documentary evidence from cryptographic proof; C2PA supplies content bindings for media integrity.

layers.name: Citation Act Provenance
layers.description: Attribution of the assertion and the distinct times that describe it.

findings.name: Asserting agent, accountability and activity
findings.description: Who or what asserted the evidential link, under which role, through which activity, and which organisation is accountable.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Agents and activities are resolved through the party and provenance models. Holding an artifact here would duplicate identity records that those models master and would drift from them as roles change.

findings.name: Time model: event, observation and ingestion
findings.description: The distinct time points a citation record must keep apart, their required form, and the validity interval of the assertion.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Timestamps are atomic values that must remain directly comparable and sortable within the record. Externalising them into an artifact would break the ordering constraints that validation depends on.

layers.name: Integrity and Verification
layers.description: Tamper-evidence over stored evidence, and independent confirmation that the citation still holds.

findings.name: Fixity of excerpt and capture, and media provenance binding
findings.description: Digests over the excerpt and the consulted representation computed after a declared canonicalization, plus references to signed media provenance manifests where the cited material is a media asset.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Digests, canonicalization profile identifiers and manifest references are compact structured values attached to the artifacts they protect. The signed manifest itself is produced, signed and validated by the media provenance system, so this model references it and never reproduces or re-issues it.

findings.name: Independent verification of the citation
findings.description: Confirmation that the citation still resolves, still anchors and still bears the stance asserted, kept distinct from cryptographic proof and from the original assertion.

bundles.name: Record Lifecycle and Governance
bundles.description: States and transitions of the citation record itself, its versioning, its stewardship, and its disposition.
bundles.rationale: The Verifiable Credentials model treats status and validity as first-class, DataCite governs versioning and obsolescence relations, and NISO CREC requires status change to propagate; a citation record therefore needs its own lifecycle distinct from either endpoint.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle
layers.description: Permitted states, transitions, versioning and supersession of the citation record.

findings.name: Citation record states and transitions
findings.description: The states a citation record may occupy, the permitted transitions between them, and what becomes immutable on assertion.
findings.inline_only_rationale: States and transitions are coded values evaluated in place on the record. Externalising them would separate the state from the data it constrains and invite the two to diverge.

findings.name: Versioning and supersession
findings.description: How corrections produce new versions, how predecessors stay resolvable, and how change is attributed.
