bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a decision or approval record is uniquely designated, versioned as expressions and manifestations, typed, and bounded in subject matter and applicability.
bundles.rationale: An agent cannot cite, deduplicate, supersede or retrieve a decision without a stable identity separated from its versions, and cannot apply the right rules without knowing the decision type and its scope of effect. ECLI proves that decision identity is a governed concern in its own right, and Akoma Ntoso proves that the decision as a work differs from its language and format versions.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: Identifier assignment for the decision act and its record, and the versioned expression structure that keeps corrections and translations distinct from the abstract decision.

findings.name: Decision and record identifier assignment
findings.description: The identifier that designates the decision, the authority that mints it, and the separation between the identifier of the decision act, the identifier of the record and any governed global identifier such as an ECLI.

findings.name: Version, expression and manifestation identity
findings.description: How successive language versions, corrected texts, consolidated texts and published formats of the same decision are distinguished without fragmenting its identity.

findings.name: Title, language and alternative names
findings.description: A short noun-phrase title representing the problem and chosen solution, plus language and any alternative citations. DCMI title and alternative apply; Nygard and MADR require a short representative heading.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Title and language are intrinsic descriptive metadata of the record, not a standalone artefact.

layers.name: Classification and subject matter
layers.description: The type of decision or approval, its binding character, and the subject matter, jurisdiction and population to which it applies.

findings.name: Decision type and binding character
findings.description: Classification of the record along the axes that change how it must be handled: decision family, binding versus advisory, interim versus final, and positive versus negative outcome.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is a set of coded attributes of the decision record itself. It produces no separate deliverable object; the controlled vocabularies it draws on are governed by the Dimension's registry links rather than by an artifact of this finding.

findings.name: Subject matter and scope of application
findings.description: What the decision is about and how far its effect reaches — addressees only or a general class, which territory or jurisdiction, and which organisational or asset scope.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject and scope are inline descriptive attributes and references to externally governed classification schemes and jurisdiction registers. Producing a separate artifact would duplicate those registers, which belong to sibling classification models.

bundles.name: Substance and reasoning
bundles.description: The decided question, the outcome and any attached conditions or obligations, together with the reasons, alternatives considered and evidence that support the outcome.
bundles.rationale: Substance and reasons are the part of a decision record that authorities most often make mandatory: 5 U.S.C. §557(c) requires findings, conclusions and reasons on all material issues, Charter Article 41(2)(c) imposes a duty to give reasons, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 requires rationale that covers alternatives not chosen. Outcome vocabularies and the obligation/advice split are given normative shape by XACML.

layers.name: Decision substance
layers.description: The question put, the disposition reached, and the conditions, obligations and implementation duties attached to it.

findings.name: Question put for decision
findings.description: The precise question, proposal, motion or request the decision resolves, including how it was framed and by whom it was brought.

findings.name: Outcome and disposition
findings.description: The operative determination: the outcome value, the order or relief granted or refused, and any non-outcome such as deferral, withdrawal or inability to decide.

findings.name: Conditions, obligations, advice and implementation duties
findings.description: What must happen for the decision to take or keep effect, what the decision obliges parties to do, what is merely advisory, and which implementation and enforcement duties follow.

layers.name: Reasoning and evidence
layers.description: The stated reasons, the alternatives weighed and rejected, and the evidence and findings of fact on which the outcome rests.

findings.name: Statement of reasons
findings.description: The reasoning that justifies the outcome, whether giving reasons is legally required for this decision, and whether the reasons form part of the operative instrument or a separate document.

findings.name: Options considered and rejected
findings.description: The alternatives evaluated, the criteria and weights applied, and the recorded justification for rejecting each alternative not chosen.

findings.name: Evidence relied upon and findings of fact
findings.description: The inputs the decision-maker used, the facts found from them, submissions received, and any communications that a rule requires to be placed on the record.

findings.name: Completeness of rulings and confirmation of implementation
findings.description: APA requires the record to show the ruling on each finding, conclusion or exception. MADR confirmation describes how implementation or compliance will be checked. Completeness is a quality property of the decision record; implementation evidence may live in sibling operational models.

bundles.name: Authority, approval and attestation
bundles.description: The competence under which the decision was taken, delegation and limits on it, the participation and voting that produced it, declared conflicts, and the evidence that fixes and attributes the record.
bundles.rationale: A decision that exceeds the decider's competence is voidable, so authority is not metadata but a validity condition. Delaware §141 supplies primary rules on quorum, committee limits, remote presence and action without a meeting; 5 U.S.C. §557 separates presiding, recommending and deciding roles; PROV-O supplies the qualified association and delegation pattern; RFC 3161 supplies third-party time attestation.

layers.name: Mandate and competence
layers.description: The source of power to decide, and the delegation instruments and thresholds that bound it.

findings.name: Decision authority and legal basis
findings.description: Which body or role held competence to take this decision, the instrument conferring that competence, and the rules of composition it had to satisfy.

findings.name: Delegation, sub-delegation and approval limits
findings.description: Where the decision was taken under delegated power, the delegation chain, its thresholds and exclusions, and its validity at the decision time.

layers.name: Approval acts, participation and objections
layers.description: The individual acts of approval, participation, voting, dissent and recusal that constitute or evidence the decision.

findings.name: Participation, quorum and vote result
findings.description: Who took part and how, whether quorum was met, how votes or consents were counted, and how decisions taken without a meeting are represented.

findings.name: Dissent, recusal and conflicts of interest
findings.description: Recorded disagreement with the outcome, withdrawals from participation on interest grounds, and declared conflicts affecting the decision's soundness.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Dissents, recusals and conflict declarations are participation events attached to the decision and are normally captured inline in the decision record or in the meeting minutes owned by WM-ACT-025. Where a dissent is issued as a standalone opinion document it is carried as an additional expression under f02 rather than as an artifact unique to this finding.

layers.name: Attestation and record integrity
layers.description: The evidence that fixes the record's content and attributes it to its signatories, and the point at which it becomes unalterable.

findings.name: Signature, seal, time-stamp and integrity evidence
findings.description: How the record is signed or sealed, how its content is fixed by digest and third-party time attestation, and how a later verifier can re-establish that it has not changed.

bundles.name: Time, validity and lifecycle
bundles.description: The distinct times attaching to a decision, the period during which it is valid, its status transitions and finality, and the ways it is superseded, revoked, challenged or annulled.
bundles.rationale: Decision records fail most often on time: a single 'decision date' cannot express that consent became effective when the last consent was delivered, that issuance and service differ, that validity is a range distinct from issuance, or that annulment operates retroactively. RFC 3339, DCMI Terms and Delaware §141(f) each supply primary support for separating these.

layers.name: Temporal frame
layers.description: The set of separately recorded times around a decision, and the validity period distinct from any of them.

findings.name: Decision event timeline
findings.description: The distinct, separately recorded moments in a decision's life — taken, consented, signed, issued, served, published, in force — plus the observation time at which each was recorded.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The timeline is a set of typed timestamp values on the decision record, each already evidenced by an artifact owned elsewhere in the model: proof of service under f25, the time-stamp token under f15 and the event-history entry under f15. Minting a separate timeline artifact would duplicate those without adding evidential weight.

findings.name: Validity window, retroactivity and expiry
findings.description: The period during which the decision is valid, whether effect reaches backwards in time, and how expiry, renewal and suspension of validity are represented.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is a temporal property of the decision expressed inline through a start, an end and suspension intervals. Where an authority issues a separate certificate of validity or currency, that is an outward-facing attestation carried by the notification artifact under f25, not a distinct object owned here.

layers.name: Lifecycle, change and challenge
layers.description: Status transitions and the point of finality, the mechanisms by which a decision is amended, replaced or undone, and the routes by which it can be challenged.

findings.name: Status model and finality
findings.description: The permitted states of a decision record, the transitions between them, and the point at which the decision becomes final and the record unalterable.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The status model is a governed enumeration and transition table applied to the record, with each transition already evidenced by the immutable event-history artifact defined under f15. Duplicating that evidence as a second artifact would create two competing audit trails.

findings.name: Supersession, amendment, corrigendum and revocation
findings.description: How a later act changes or displaces this decision, distinguishing correction of the text from amendment of the substance and from withdrawal of the decision itself.

findings.name: Challenge, appeal, review and annulment
findings.description: The routes by which the decision can be contested, the time limits and suspensive effects that apply, and how the outcome of a challenge is recorded against the original.

findings.name: Adjudicative grade and conclusiveness
findings.description: In hearings under APA § 557, a presiding employee may issue an initial decision that becomes the agency decision unless appealed or reviewed; otherwise a recommended or tentative decision may be required, except where the agency finds on the record that due and timely execution of its functions imperatively and unavoidably requires omission.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Grade and conclusiveness are legal-state fields of the record. The supporting finding of imperative omission, if any, is text on this record rather than a new artefact type.

bundles.name: Relational context
bundles.description: The links that place a decision in its wider setting — the matter, occasion and prior decisions that produced it, and the parties and objects it acts upon.
bundles.rationale: A decision record with no outward links cannot be audited, aggregated or enforced. PROV-O supplies the generic derivation and association links, ECLI's metadata expectations imply citation links between decisions, and the registry's own CONTAINS and COMPOSE relations to the meeting and administrative-case models require explicit linkage semantics on this side.

layers.name: Contextual linkage
layers.description: Typed relationships from the decision to its procedural context, related decisions, addressees and subject objects.

findings.name: Relationships to matter, occasion and other decisions
findings.description: Typed links to the case or matter, the meeting or consent process that produced the decision, and prior, related, implementing and cited decisions.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are typed references to objects owned by other models — the meeting by WM-ACT-025, the case by WM-POL-017, and other decisions by further instances of this model. Materialising them as an artifact would create a second, divergent copy of relationships that the referenced models already hold authoritatively.

findings.name: Addressees, affected parties and subject objects
findings.description: Who the decision is addressed to, who else it affects, and which concrete objects — assets, applications, permits, budgets, systems — it operates on.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Addressees and subject objects are references into party, asset and application models that own their master data. This finding governs only the linkage and the effect characterisation; holding a local artifact would duplicate party master data and create an unmanaged personal-data copy.

findings.name: Generating activity, used entities and derivation
findings.description: A decision record is a PROV entity generated by a deciding activity that used submissions, evidence, prior decisions, models or meeting records. Derivation and revision relate a later record to an earlier one without implying that usage alone is sufficient. Bundles support provenance of provenance.

bundles.name: Automated and assisted decisioning
bundles.description: How much of the decision was made by a machine, which system and configuration produced it, and what human oversight, explanation and contestability attach as a result.
bundles.rationale: Where a decision is taken wholly or partly by a system, additional and legally consequential context becomes mandatory: the system's identity and version, the logic applied, human oversight, and the affected person's right to intervention, to express a point of view and to contest. GDPR Article 22, the Article 29 Working Party guidance and the AI Act's oversight and logging duties all attach to this distinction, and XACML supplies the structure of a machine-rendered decision result.

layers.name: Automation, oversight and explanation
layers.description: Decision mode and system attribution, and the oversight, explanation and contest mechanisms triggered by automation.

findings.name: Decision mode and system attribution
findings.description: Whether the decision was human, system-assisted or solely automated, and which system, model, policy version and inputs produced or shaped the result.

findings.name: Human oversight, explanation and contestability
findings.description: The oversight measures applied to an automated or assisted decision, the explanation owed to the affected person, and the mechanisms for intervention and contest.

bundles.name: Disclosure, retention and interoperability
bundles.description: How the decision is published or served, who may access which parts under what redactions, how long it is kept and how it is disposed of, and how it is expressed for exchange with external systems.
bundles.rationale: A decision that is not communicated may not take effect, and one that is over-disclosed breaches confidentiality and personal-data duties. Charter Article 41(2)(b) grants file access subject to confidentiality; NARA's ERM requirements and MoReq2010 supply disposal, transfer and hold mechanics; ECLI, Akoma Ntoso, DCMI and PROV supply the exchange vocabularies.

layers.name: Disclosure, notification and access
layers.description: Proactive publication and individual service, access classification, redaction and anonymisation.

findings.name: Publication, notification and service
findings.description: How the decision is made known — published to a register or the public, and served on or notified to addressees — and the proof that communication occurred.

findings.name: Access classification, confidentiality and redaction
findings.description: Who may see which parts of the record, what must be withheld or anonymised, and how a party's right to access their own file is reconciled with confidentiality.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and external alignment
layers.description: How long the decision record is kept and how it is disposed of or transferred, and how it is projected into external identifier schemes and vocabularies.

findings.name: Retention trigger, disposition and disposal hold
findings.description: The event that starts the retention clock for a decision, the authorised disposition outcome, and the holds that suspend disposal.

findings.name: External alignment, identifiers and exchange projection
findings.description: How the decision record maps to external identifier schemes and vocabularies for exchange, and which mappings are lossy, conflicting or unsupported.

model.name: Taxonomy / Classification Scheme
model.purpose: Represent one governed versioned knowledge-organization scheme containing concept definitions, labels, notations, semantic relations, mappings and release governance.
model.scope_statement: Owns scheme identity, namespace, canonical URI, profile, purpose, scope, subject, audience, language, jurisdiction, owner, publisher and steward; immutable releases and change sets; concept identity, scheme membership and top concepts; labels, definitions, notes, examples and notations; broader, narrower and related relations; hierarchy profiles, polyhierarchy, facets, arrays, collections and ordered membership; cross-scheme mappings with versions, method, confidence and provenance; proposal, approval, publication, deprecation, replacement, split, merge and retirement; validation, quality, access, licensing, retention and loss-aware projections. Classified real-world objects, classification bindings, source evidence, policies, workflows, datasets and search indexes remain external.
in_scope: Scheme identity, namespace, profile, scope, authority, release and concept membership
Labels, definitions, notations, hierarchy, association, facets, collections, mappings, lifecycle and validation
Provenance, governance, access, licensing, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning classified objects, classification bindings, evidence, organization, policy, workflow, dataset or search-index lifecycles
Equating labels with identity, concepts with referents, broader with part-of, closeMatch with exactMatch, or mapping with proved equivalence
Executing release approval, object reassignment, protected disclosure, external system mutation or irreversible deletion without authority

boundary_notes.distinction: A classification binding assigns an external object to a concept in a pinned scheme release. The scheme defines that concept; the registry parent direction appears reversed or navigational and remains held for review.
A concept is a unit of thought or authority entry with its own URI. The person, place, product or other referent remains a separate mastered object.
OWL and RDFS can express formal class axioms while SHACL validates graphs. A taxonomy may project to them but does not inherit formal semantics unless the profile declares them.
ISO/IEC 11179 defines generic registration, identification, designation, definition, classification and mapping facilities. This model specializes them for a knowledge-organization scheme.
DCAT, DataCite and RO-Crate distributions package or describe a release. They do not replace canonical scheme, concept or mapping identity.
An index may tokenize labels and materialize hierarchy for retrieval. Ranking, cache, deployment and query-log lifecycles remain external.
The scheme owns mapping assertions and their status, while evidence and reviewer decisions remain attributable external records. Mapping never silently merges concept identity.

preconditions: active Dimension
namespace authority

functions.description: Create or revise one concept with stable identity, definition, characteristics and scheme membership.

referent boundary declared

functions.description: Append language-tagged preferred, alternative or hidden labels, notes and typed notations.
preconditions: language and uniqueness rules pass

functions.name: Relate concepts
functions.description: Append typed broader, narrower, related or custom semantic relations with explicit hierarchy profile.
preconditions: endpoints and profile resolvable

functions.name: Manage facets and collections
functions.description: Create facets, arrays, collections, ordered membership and compound structures without changing concept identity.
preconditions: membership and ordering valid
effects: grouping remains distinct from semantic hierarchy

functions.name: Map schemes
functions.description: Append source-qualified cross-scheme mappings with exact semantics, versions, method and confidence.
preconditions: scheme versions pinned
effects: identity is not merged and weak mappings do not gain stronger inference

functions.name: Validate scheme
functions.description: Run identity, lexical, structural, mapping, quality and profile checks against a pinned release.
preconditions: validator and profile pinned
effects: results remain distinct from editorial approval

functions.description: Review a proposal, append approval or rejection and issue an immutable release and change set.
preconditions: separation of duties
release gate passes

functions.description: Append deprecation and successor relations while retaining old identifiers and affected-binding impact.
preconditions: change authority
impact assessed

functions.description: Produce an authorized version-pinned standards projection with declared loss and round-trip limits.
preconditions: authorized recipient
target pinned

composition.purpose: Resolve assignments of external objects to concepts while the registry parent direction remains under review.

composition.target: Classified object, evidence, policy, dataset, distribution and search-index masters
composition.purpose: Resolve external referents, sources, governance and delivery context without importing their lifecycles.
Project concepts, schemes, labels, notations, notes, semantic relations, collections, mappings and integrity conditions.
Project linked-data classes, properties, axioms, annotations, contexts, language maps and graph serialization.
Project validation, attribution, revision, invalidation and quality measurement semantics.
Project catalog, distribution, persistent metadata and portable release packaging views.
Project multilingual thesaurus construction, maintenance, exchange and cross-vocabulary mapping profiles.
Project terminology, concept, designation, definition and controlled-vocabulary management profiles.

composition.target: DCMI Metadata Terms and Library of Congress MADS/RDF
composition.purpose: Project vocabulary metadata, authority data, variants, schemes, collections and RWO separation.
Project language-tag identity, validation, filtering and lookup for labels and notes.
Project rights constraints, unambiguous clocks and deterministic JSON serialization.
Project registry-item identification, designation, definition, registration, classification and mapping facilities.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner, scheme owner, publisher, vocabulary steward, concept editors, mapping reviewers, release approvers and access roles.
Register authoritative scheme, concept, label, notation, relation, mapping, status, language, license, validation and projection profiles.
Register classified-object and classification-binding masters separately from scheme content.
Pin subject, language, jurisdiction, reasoning, validation, serialization and exchange profiles.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint scheme, release, concept, label assertion, relation, collection, mapping, proposal, validation and projection identifiers only in the adopting Dimension namespace; preserve classified-object, binding, evidence, policy, dataset and index identities as typed external references.
registry_links: https://ver.cy/models/
https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md
Dimension-local scheme, namespace, language, relation, mapping, status, license, access, retention and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, authoritative scheme identifier and namespace, immutable release, concept URI, assertion identity, owner and source; never use a label, notation, path, filename or hash alone as identity.
Keep scheme, concept, label, notation, semantic relation, collection, mapping, classified object and classification binding distinct.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, relation semantics, language, authority, source, rationale, access, time and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new release, immutable change set, migration and mapping files, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior URIs and assignments.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when scheme and concept identity, labels, definitions, relation semantics, mapping, lifecycle and access meaning remain intact.
SKOS, RDF, RDFS, OWL, JSON-LD, MADS, DCMI, DCAT, DataCite and RO-Crate mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted, inferred or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for the scheme, concept, mapping, release or change assertion.
Governed globally resolvable scheme or concept IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep proposal, review, approval, issue, effective, publication, deprecation, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {scheme-id}--{artifact-kind}--{release-or-assertion-id}; never use a date, title, label, notation, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, namespace, source and vocabulary versions, language, scope, clocks, provenance, assurance, license and access marking for each retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may register namespaces, define concepts, manage labels, assert relations, create mappings, validate, approve releases, deprecate, disclose, retain and tombstone scheme records.

Every published release requires stable scheme and concept identities, namespace, profile, purpose, scope, owner, labels, definitions, relation semantics, change set, validation and provenance as applicable.
Agents never infer concept identity from a label or code, part-of from broader, equivalence from close mapping, or universal authority from publication.
Classified objects, classification bindings, source evidence, policies, datasets and indexes remain external masters.

Automated agents may append low-risk candidate mappings, lexical checks and projections under delegation, but namespace creation, release approval, destructive change and protected disclosure require accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, scheme and release, language, hierarchy and mapping inference profile, assurance, license and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable scheme and concept identities, namespace, profile, scope, owner, language and explicit unknowns before adding labels, relations or mappings.
update: Append an immutable label, definition, relation, mapping, lifecycle or correction assertion with actor, authority, reason, source, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor.
delete: Apply policy, licensing, dispute, assignment-impact, audit, retention and legal-hold rules; tombstone eligible scheme-owned assertions while preserving URI resolution, material provenance and non-cascading external bindings.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Own namespace, mastership, delegation, access, retention and federation rules.

roles.name: Scheme owner or publisher
responsibilities: Own purpose, scope, authority, releases, license and public commitments.

roles.name: Vocabulary steward
responsibilities: Own scheme profile, concept model, relation semantics, lifecycle and editorial policy.

roles.name: Concept editor or terminologist
responsibilities: Propose identifiers, definitions, labels, notations, notes and internal relations.

roles.name: Mapping curator
responsibilities: Own mapping methods, evidence, confidence, review and conflict handling.

roles.name: Release approver
responsibilities: Own change-set acceptance, validation gate, effective time and publication decision.

roles.name: Consumer or classifier
responsibilities: Use pinned releases and keep external classification bindings in their owning model.

roles.name: Reviewer or auditor
responsibilities: Review authority, quality, mappings, changes, access and retention without rewriting originals.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless active Dimension, role, purpose, scheme sensitivity, jurisdiction, license and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary projection.
exceptions: Emergency or legally compelled access must be grounded, time-limited, purpose-bound, attributable, independently reviewed and unable to erase immutable scheme, release, mapping, dispute or legal-hold evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, role, purpose, scheme and release identity, action, decision, policy and vocabulary versions, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected concepts or mappings, source evidence and outcome for privileged mutation or disclosure.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, active scheme, release, language, hierarchy and mapping profile, authorities, license, access and retention rules.
Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required classification-binding, evidence, policy, dataset and index instructions before mutation.

coverage.claim: WM-KNW-018 covers a governed versioned Taxonomy / Classification Scheme with scheme and concept identity, namespace, profile, scope, labels, definitions, notations, hierarchy, associations, facets, collections, mappings, lifecycle, change sets, governance, validation, quality, rights, retention and loss-aware interoperability. Domain, language, licensing, reasoning and independent-review questions remain deferred.

checklist.notes: Scheme, release, concept, label assertion, relation, mapping, proposal, validation and successor identities remain distinct.
Taxonomy, thesaurus, classification, controlled list, synonym ring, ontology and hybrid profiles are explicit.
Namespace, purpose, scope, language, labels, definitions, notations, relations, mappings, status and license are covered.
Agents distinguish concepts through stable URIs, definitions, characteristics, scheme membership and profile rules rather than labels alone.
Draft, approved, published, deprecated, superseded and retired scheme and concept states preserve releases and change sets.
Hierarchy, association, collections, mappings, successors and external classification bindings use typed relations.
Proposal, approval, issue, effective, publication, deprecation, correction and ingestion clocks remain distinct.
Geographic scope and jurisdiction are represented when a vocabulary is location-bound; geometry remains external.
Sources, editors, mappers, methods, evidence, decisions, changes, validations and releases are linked.
Scheme authority, concept editorship, mapping responsibility, release approval and object classification are not conflated.
Identity, language, label, notation, hierarchy, cycles, mappings, shapes, quality and migration checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, license, sensitivity, minimum projection and audit are represented.
Deprecation, dispute, assignment impact, legal hold, URI continuity and tombstones are non-cascading.
SKOS, RDF, OWL, JSON-LD, MADS, DCMI, DCAT, DataCite and RO-Crate mappings disclose inference and loss.
Registration, definition, labeling, relating, grouping, mapping, validation, release, replacement and projection declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Domain, language, jurisdiction, legal, safety, privacy, licensing, reasoning and retention profiles require expert review.
Classified objects, classification bindings, evidence, policies, datasets, search indexes and operational workflows remain neighboring masters.
Automatic concept induction, universal mapping, ontology theorem proving and silent reassignment after taxonomy change remain future work.
conflicts: SKOS broader is an informal semantic relation and does not universally distinguish generic, instance and partitive hierarchy, so explicit profiles are required.
SKOS exactMatch is transitive while closeMatch is not; neither should silently become OWL sameAs or object identity.
Taxonomies, thesauri, classifications, authority files and formal ontologies differ in semantics, governance and inference and cannot share one universal conformance profile.
regional_assumptions: ISO and NISO vocabulary standards, W3C linked-data vocabularies and Library of Congress authority data are complementary profiles rather than universal law.
Labels, definitions, preferred terms, mapping judgments and publication authority depend on language, community, discipline and jurisdiction.
ISO 25964 parts are under revision and licensed details require exact release pins before production conformance claims.
adversarial_checks: Reject a scheme or concept without stable authoritative identity, namespace, release, owner, source and lifecycle state.

decisions.concept: Taxonomy / Classification Scheme aggregate boundary
decisions.rationale: The scheme owns its governed concept graph and release history while classified objects, assignments, evidence, policy and search infrastructure remain external.

decisions.concept: WM-XCT-020 parent signal
decisions.rationale: A classification binding normally points to a concept in a scheme, so parentage in the opposite direction may be navigational or reversed and cannot be approved from the frozen ledger.

decisions.concept: Concept versus real-world referent
decisions.rationale: Stable concept identity, definition and labels do not replace the person, place, product or other object classified by that concept.

decisions.concept: Hierarchy profiles
decisions.rationale: Generic, instance, partitive and informal broader relations have different semantics; transitivity, cycles and polyhierarchy must be declared and validated per profile.

decisions.concept: Exact, close and formal equivalence
decisions.rationale: SKOS exactMatch, closeMatch, OWL sameAs, equivalentClass and registry mappings have different inferential consequences and never silently merge identity.

decisions.concept: Labels, notations and identity
decisions.rationale: Language-tagged labels and typed notations are mutable designations; canonical concept URIs and authoritative identifiers remain the identity anchors.

decisions.concept: Deprecation, split, merge and migration
decisions.rationale: Every structural change retains prior releases, successor mappings, impact on external bindings and resolvable identifiers rather than silently rewriting history.

decisions.concept: Standards projections
decisions.rationale: SKOS, RDF, OWL, JSON-LD, MADS, DCMI, DCAT, DataCite and RO-Crate projections pin versions and disclose inference and round-trip loss.

decisions.concept: Automated operation boundary
decisions.rationale: Agents may append low-risk candidate mappings and checks but namespace creation, release approval, destructive change and protected disclosure require authority.

decisions.concept: Provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet attempt timed out and one bounded Grok attempt returned provider error 402. Codex separately audits the frozen validated result and comparison without acquiring new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet attempt timed out and one Grok attempt returned provider error 402 before producing an admissible result; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-XCT-020 remains a reference because the registered parent direction appears navigational or reversed and requires joint boundary review.
Boundary hold: classified objects, classification bindings, evidence, organizations, policies, workflows, datasets and search indexes remain external masters.
Hierarchy hold: generic, instance, partitive and informal broader relations require explicit inference, cycle and polyhierarchy profiles.
Mapping hold: exactMatch, closeMatch, sameAs, equivalentClass and registry mapping semantics remain distinct and source-target versions must be pinned.
Language hold: multilingual labels require current BCP 47 registry validation, editorial policy and language-specific review.
Licensing hold: ISO and other licensed vocabulary profiles require legal review before reproducing protected structures or claiming conformance.
Interoperability hold: every standards projection requires exact release pins, conformance tests, round-trip tests and semantic-loss declarations.
Completeness hold: the 24-source draft is broad but does not claim universal domain, linguistic, ontological, legal or operational coverage.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Resolve whether the WM-XCT-020 Classification Binding parent signal is navigational, reversed or should be replaced by an outbound reference from the binding to the scheme.
Develop domain-specific taxonomy, thesaurus, classification, ontology, multilingual, hierarchy, facet and mapping profiles.
Pin ISO 25964 replacements and every production crosswalk to exact releases and run bidirectional conformance, inference and semantic-loss tests.
Obtain independent terminology, library science, ontology, domain, accessibility, legal, privacy, security and records review.

EM-KNW-01.content:
# EM-KNW-01 local synthesis

## Disposition

- Create an **Enterprise document, knowledge and terminology profile** over WM-REC-001, WM-KNW-006 and WM-KNW-018.
- Do not create a new catalogue or runtime identifier.
- Treat Knowledge Article as a document/record designation and Term Definition as concept-owned descriptive content, not independent aggregate roots.
- Route independently identified assertions and decisions to EM-KNW-02 rather than expanding this contour.

## Aggregate boundaries

WM-REC-001 owns the stable record identity, immutable version chain, instantiations, custody, evidence and disposition. A URL, file or carrier is a location or instantiation, never the record identity. Document Revision remains owned by the record because retention, holds, supersession and last-copy rules span the full aggregate.

WM-KNW-006 owns a concept's persistent identity and intrinsic meaning: delimitation, characteristics, definitions with sources, designations with language/script/context, global deprecation, merge/split and successor continuity. A concept remains valid and citable outside any scheme.

WM-KNW-018 owns scheme identity, namespace, immutable releases and every release-scoped assertion: membership, top concept, in-scheme relations, facets, collections and mappings. It references pinned concept versions; it does not become a second master for intrinsic concept content.

## Ownership rule

If an assertion loses its meaning when the scheme release is removed, the scheme masters it. If it survives removal from every scheme, the concept masters it. Every assertion has one editable master; concept-side membership/relation views are derived and read-only.

Concept retirement and scheme-local withdrawal are different operations. Retirement preserves the globally resolvable concept identifier and successor guidance. Withdrawal removes a concept from a scheme release without deprecating it elsewhere.

## Required profile constraints

1. A document classification binding pins concept IRI and exact scheme release; a label alone cannot classify a record.
2. A new URL or storage system creates a new location/instantiation reference and, only after a fixing event, possibly a new version. It does not create new knowledge identity.
3. Content digest proves byte state, not document or concept identity.
4. Concept equality requires an authorised identity/mapping assertion with basis and context. Lexical equality never establishes same-as.
5. Definitions retain source, provenance, language, subject field, jurisdiction/audience context, status and dispute state. Disputed does not mean deprecated.
6. Scheme-less concepts are allowed; release binding must therefore be optional or point to a concept-register release rather than an unrelated scheme release.
7. Published record versions and scheme releases are append-only and never renumbered.

## Acceptance result

A migrated document keeps its record identifier and complete version sequence. The target system ID becomes an alternate identifier with assertion provenance; format conversion is a derived instantiation with its own digest and event. Existing signatures remain bound to their original bytes.

Two identical words in distinct subject fields remain two concepts. Two competing definitions may remain on one concept only when their intension is the same and each definition retains its authority and context; otherwise they identify distinct concepts. No silent merge or preferred winner is inferred.

## Holds

All three bases are reviewable drafts with `publishableCanonical: false`. WM-KNW-006 and WM-KNW-018 have independent-review waivers; WM-REC-001 retains source/version and cross-profile holds. WM-KNW-006 and WM-KNW-018 currently overlap in ownership text, their registry relationship is unresolved, and definition-level access/dispute semantics need amendment. This checkpoint is research evidence, not an installable release.

EM-KNW-02.content:
# EM-KNW-02 local synthesis

## Disposition

- Create an **Enterprise decision, claim and evidence profile** over WM-KNW-010, WM-REC-010, WM-KNW-007 and WM-KNW-008.
- Do not create a profile runtime ID.
- Raise **Evidence Artifact / Source Work** as a genuine new-model candidate with identifier unassigned. The four reserved models intentionally do not master the cited item itself.

## Boundary and ownership

WM-KNW-007 masters claim identity, statement, scope, asserter, commitment, confidence and claim lifecycle. WM-KNW-008 masters the reified citation relationship: citing context, cited source reference, stance, locator, consulted representation, verification and source-status observations. A citation is not evidence truth.

WM-KNW-010 masters decision content: question, alternatives, exclusion reasons, criteria, evaluations, selection, conditions, rationale, arguments, objections and dissent. WM-REC-010 masters the authentic issued expression: fixation, signature/seal, issuance, publication/service evidence, record finality timestamps, redacted expressions and records disposition.

Duplicated REC-010 text fields are version-pinned transcriptions of WM-KNW-010 content. They are never independent authoring fields. Content changes create a successor decision and a successor fixed expression.

## Required profile constraints

1. WM-KNW-010 evidence bindings resolve to WM-KNW-008 citation IDs. Locator, stance and citation type remain read-only projections from WM-KNW-008.
2. Every argument premise/conclusion resolves to a pinned WM-KNW-007 claim or is explicitly marked as a local restatement.
3. Observation/source material, citation stance, claim assessment and decision-local appraisal remain separate.
4. Alternative sets, evaluation rounds, objections and dissent are append-only.
5. WM-KNW-010 declares challenge rules; WM-REC-010 owns service events and computed finality dates.
6. Revocation, annulment, reopening or later counter-evidence never erases earlier rationale or fixed expressions.
7. ADR is a lightweight WM-KNW-010 profile and need not create a formal WM-REC-010 instrument unless one is issued.

## Acceptance result

Two decisions may use separate citations to the same source artifact. If that source is later retracted, each citation receives an append-only status observation and verification report. Related claims retain their canonical statements and gain status-notice/conflict references. Each decision rechecks its own premise support and sensitivity. One may reopen and produce a successor decision while the other remains effective. Original outcomes, alternatives, dissent and fixed records remain resolvable.

The negative case fails: a link to a document supplies only a source reference and citation stance. It cannot turn the citing claim into an established fact.

## Evidence Artifact candidate

The cited work or evidence item has identity and lifecycle independent of every claim, citation and decision. It may be cited many times, corrected, retracted, superseded or preserved while all citation acts remain intact. WM-KNW-008 explicitly caches only a non-authoritative descriptor. This proves a missing aggregate boundary, but no registry identifier is allocated, so the candidate remains research-only.

## Holds

All four existing models remain `publishableCanonical: false`. Their relation ledgers do not yet support the proposed binding; WM-KNW-008 deduplication is insufficiently specified; several serial artefact identities are ambiguous; and three bases carry a single-provider waiver. Evidence Artifact requires registry allocation and its own source/bibliographic/record boundary review. This checkpoint is not an installable release.
